sentences.zh: 崔祖思

translations.literal: Cui Zusi
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zusi

sentences.zh: 崔祖思字敬元，清河東武城人，崔琰七世孫也。

translations.literal: Cui Zusi, styled Jingyuan, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe; he was the seventh-generation descendant of Cui Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zusi, styled Jingyuan, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe, seventh in descent from Cui Yan.

sentences.zh: 祖諲，宋冀州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shen was Inspector of Ji under the Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shen served as inspector of Ji under the Song.

sentences.zh: 父僧護，州秀才。

translations.literal: His father Senghu was a provincial scholar-recommended candidate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Senghu was a provincial scholar nominee.

sentences.zh: 祖思少有志氣，好讀書史。

translations.literal: As a youth Zusi had ambition and loved reading histories.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Zusi had spirit and loved histories.

sentences.zh: 初州辟主簿，與刺史劉懷珍於堯廟祠神，廟有蘇侯像。

translations.literal: At first the province recruited him as chief clerk; with the inspector Liu Huaizhen he sacrificed to the gods at the Yao temple, which had an image of Lord Su.
translations.idiomatic: At first the province took him as chief clerk; with Inspector Liu Huaizhen he sacrificed at the Yao temple, where there stood an image of Lord Su.

sentences.zh: 懷珍曰：「堯聖人，而與雜神爲列，欲去之，何如？

translations.literal: Huaizhen said: 「Yao was a sage, yet here he stands ranked with miscellaneous spirits—we mean to remove them; what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen said: 「Yao was a sage, yet he is set in one row with stray gods—we wish to take them away; what say you?

sentences.zh: 」祖思曰：「蘇峻今日可謂四凶之五也。

translations.literal: 」Zusi said: 「Su Jun today may be called a fifth of the Four Evils.
translations.idiomatic: 」Zusi said: 「Su Jun today is a fifth among the Four Evils.

sentences.zh: 」懷珍遂令除諸雜神。

translations.literal: 」Huaizhen then ordered all miscellaneous spirits removed.
translations.idiomatic: 」Huaizhen then had every stray god cleared away.

sentences.zh: 太祖在淮陰，祖思聞風自結，爲上輔國主簿，甚見親待，參豫謀議。

translations.literal: When the Founder was at Huaiyin, Zusi heard of his renown and attached himself, serving the Founder as chief clerk of the Supporter-of-State staff; he was greatly favored and took part in counsel.
translations.idiomatic: While the Founder was at Huaiyin, Zusi heard his fame and bound himself to him, serving as chief clerk on the supporter-of-state staff; he was warmly trusted and joined in planning.

sentences.zh: 除奉朝請，安成王撫軍行參軍，員外正員郎，冀州中正。

translations.literal: He was made irregular attendant-at-court, acting staff officer on the pacification-army staff of the Prince of Ancheng, supernumerary full gentleman, and Ji Province impartial nominee.
translations.idiomatic: He was named irregular attendant-at-court, acting staff officer on the pacification-army staff of the Prince of Ancheng, supernumerary full gentleman, and impartial nominee for Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 宋朝初議封太祖爲梁公，祖思啓太祖曰：「讖書云『金刀利刃齊刈之』。

translations.literal: When the Song at first debated enfeoffing the Founder as Duke of Liang, Zusi addressed the Founder: 「The prophecy book says, 『The golden blade's sharp edge—Qi shall cut it down.』
translations.idiomatic: When the Song first debated enfeoffing the Founder as duke of Liang, Zusi wrote to him: 「The prophecy book says, 『The golden blade's sharp edge—Qi shall cut it down.』

sentences.zh: 今宜稱齊，實應天命。

translations.literal: Now you should take the name Qi; this truly answers Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Now you should bear the name Qi; that truly answers Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: 」The court followed his counsel.

sentences.zh: 轉爲相國從事中郎，遷齊國內史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to senior staff officer of the chancellor-of-state, and moved to interior minister of Qi state.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to senior staff officer of the chancellor-of-state and made interior minister of the state of Qi.

sentences.zh: ，轉長兼給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: , and transferred as chief administrator concurrently supernumerary attendant of the yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred as chief administrator concurrently supernumerary attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 上初卽位，祖思啓陳政事曰：

translations.literal: When the Emperor first took the throne, Zusi memorialized on government affairs, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor first took the throne, Zusi memorialized on state affairs, saying:

sentences.zh: :　　「《禮誥》者，人倫之襟冕，帝王之樞柄。

translations.literal: : 「The Rites and Proclamations are the collar and cap of human relations, the hinge of kingship.
translations.idiomatic: 「The Rites and Proclamations are the collar and cap of human bonds, the hinge of kingship.

sentences.zh: 自古開物成務，必以教學爲先。

translations.literal: From antiquity, to open the world and accomplish tasks, teaching and learning must come first.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, to open the world and finish the work, teaching and learning have come first.

sentences.zh: 世不習學，民忘志義，悖競因斯而興，禍亂是焉而作。

translations.literal: When the age does not practice learning, the people forget purpose and right conduct; violent rivalry rises from this, and disaster and rebellion spring from it.
translations.idiomatic: When the age does not study, the people forget purpose and duty; reckless strife rises from it, and ruin and revolt are born there.

sentences.zh: 故篤俗昌治，莫先道教，不得以夷險革慮，儉泰移業。

translations.literal: Therefore to secure custom and flourish governance, nothing precedes the Way of teaching; one may not alter one's intent for ease or hardship, nor shift one's calling for want or abundance.
translations.idiomatic: To deepen custom and brighten rule, nothing comes before the teaching of the Way; one must not change one's resolve for danger or ease, nor shift one's trade for thrift or excess.

sentences.zh: 今無員之官，空受祿力。

translations.literal: Now offices without quotas empty receive salary and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Today posts without quotas draw pay and corvée in vain.

sentences.zh: 三載無考績之效，九年闕登黜之序。

translations.literal: Three years pass without the effect of performance review; nine years lack the sequence of promotion and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Three years bring no fruit of performance review; nine years lack the order of rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 國儲以之虛匱，民力爲之凋散。

translations.literal: State stores grow hollow from it; the people's strength is scattered by it.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury grows empty from it; the people's strength is thinned by it.

sentences.zh: 能否無章，涇渭混流。

translations.literal: Ability and inability go unmarked; Jing and Wei mingle in one stream.
translations.idiomatic: Able and unable go unmarked; clear and muddy run in one stream.

sentences.zh: 宜大廟之南，弘脩文序；

translations.literal: South of the grand temple, magnify the schools of letters;
translations.idiomatic: South of the grand temple, broaden the schools of letters;

sentences.zh: 司農以北，廣開武校。

translations.literal: north of the Minister of Revenue, broadly open military academies.
translations.idiomatic: north of the minister of revenue, open military academies far and wide.

sentences.zh: 臺府州國，限外之職，問其所樂，依方課習，各盡其能。

translations.literal: Ministries, prefectures, and princedoms—for posts outside the quota, ask what each delights in, assign study by specialty, and let each exhaust his capacity.
translations.idiomatic: In the ministries, prefectures, and princedoms, for posts beyond the quota ask what each man loves, set study by specialty, and let each spend his gift.

sentences.zh: 月供僮幹，如先充給。

translations.literal: Monthly supply of bond-servants and runners as before for support.
translations.idiomatic: Each month supply bond-servants and runners as before for their keep.

sentences.zh: 若有廢墮，遣還故郡。

translations.literal: If any fall idle, send them back to their home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: If any fail and fall idle, send them back to their home commandery.

sentences.zh: 殊經奇藝，待以不次，士脩其業，必有異等，民識其利，能無勉勵。」

translations.literal: For unusual classics and rare arts, treat with extraordinary promotion; when gentlemen cultivate their craft there will surely be outstanding ranks, and when the people see the profit they cannot fail to be urged onward.」
translations.idiomatic: For rare classics and wondrous arts, advance them out of turn; when scholars polish their craft there will surely be outstanding ranks, and when the people see the gain they cannot but strive.」

sentences.zh: :　　又曰：「漢文集上書囊以爲殿帷，身衣弋綈，以韋帶劔，慎夫人衣不曳地，惜中人十家之產，不爲露臺。

translations.literal: : Also he said: 「The Han emperor gathered the bags that held memorials to use as hall curtains, wore crude silk himself, belted his sword with leather cord; Lady Shen's robes did not trail the ground; he prized the property of ten middle households and would not build a terrace in the open.
translations.idiomatic: Also he said: 「Emperor Wen of Han piled the bags that held memorials to make hall curtains, wore plain silk himself, and belted his sword with leather; Lady Shen's skirts did not sweep the floor; he spared the wealth of ten palace households and would not raise an open terrace.

sentences.zh: 劉備取帳鉤銅鑄錢以充國用。

translations.literal: Liu Bei took bronze from tent-hooks to cast coin and fill the state's needs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei took bronze from tent-hooks to cast coin and fill the treasury.

sentences.zh: 魏武遣女，皁帳，婢十人，東阿婦以繡衣賜死，王景興以淅米見誚。

translations.literal: Wei Wu when sending off a daughter gave only a black-lacquer tent and ten maidservants; the Lady of Dong'e was ordered to die for embroidered robes; Wang Jingxing was mocked for rinsed rice.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao, when marrying off a daughter, sent only a black-lacquer tent and ten maids; the Lady of Dong'e was ordered to die for embroidered robes; Wang Lang was mocked for rinsed rice.

sentences.zh: 宋武節儉過人，張妃房唯碧綃蚊幬，三齊穀席，五盞盤桃花米飯。

translations.literal: Song Wu surpassed men in frugality: Consort Zhang's chamber had only blue silk mosquito nets, a mat of grain from the three Qi districts, and peach-blossom rice in a five-bowl dish.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Song was thriftier than other men: Consort Zhang's room held only blue silk mosquito nets, a mat of grain from the three Qi, and peach-blossom rice in a five-bowl dish.

sentences.zh: 殷仲文勸令畜伎，荅云『我不解聲』。

translations.literal: Yin Zhongwen urged him to keep entertainers; he answered, 『I do not understand music.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhongwen urged him to keep musicians; he answered, 『I do not understand sound.

sentences.zh: 仲文曰『但畜自解』，又荅『畏解，故不畜』。

translations.literal: Zhongwen said, 『Keep them and you will understand by yourself』; he answered again, 『I fear understanding—therefore I do not keep them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen said, 『Keep them and you will understand on your own』; he answered again, 『I fear understanding—so I do not keep them.

sentences.zh: 歷觀帝王，未嘗不以約素興，侈麗亡也。

translations.literal: Surveying emperors through the ages, none ever failed to rise through restraint and plainness, or perish through extravagance and splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Looking across emperors of every age, none ever failed to rise through plain restraint or fall through lavish excess.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下，體唐成儉，踵虞爲樸。

translations.literal: I bow before Your Majesty, who takes Yao and Tang's thrift as your body and treads Shun's plainness in your footsteps.
translations.idiomatic: I bow before Your Majesty, who take Yao and Tang for thrift and tread Shun for plainness.

sentences.zh: 寢殿則素木卑構，膳器則陶瓢充御。

translations.literal: The sleeping hall is plain wood built low; the dining vessels are clay ladles enough for the court.
translations.idiomatic: The sleeping hall is plain wood built low; the dining vessels are clay ladles enough for the court.

sentences.zh: 瓊簪玉箸，碎以爲塵，珍裘繡服，焚之如草。

translations.literal: Jade hairpins and ivory chopsticks are crushed to dust; precious furs and embroidered robes are burned like grass.
translations.idiomatic: Jade hairpins and ivory chopsticks are ground to dust; precious furs and embroidered robes are burned like grass.

sentences.zh: 斯實風高上代，民偃下世矣。

translations.literal: This truly lifts the wind of high antiquity and lets the people rest in an age below.
translations.idiomatic: This truly raises the wind of high antiquity and lets the people lie down in a later age.

sentences.zh: 然教信雖孚，氓染未革，宜加甄明，以速歸厚。

translations.literal: Yet though teaching's faith is deep, the common folk's dye is not yet changed; distinction should be added to clarify, to hasten return to substance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though teaching's faith is deep, the people's stain is not yet washed away; you should clarify ranks to hurry them back to substance.

sentences.zh: 詳察朝士，有柴車蓬館，高以殊等；

translations.literal: Examine court gentlemen closely: where there are brushwood carts and rush-thatched lodges, raise their special rank;
translations.idiomatic: Look closely at court gentlemen: where there are brushwood carts and rush-thatched inns, raise their special rank;

sentences.zh: 雕墻華輪，卑其稱謂。

translations.literal: where there are carved walls and splendid wheels, lower their titles of honor.
translations.idiomatic: where there are carved walls and splendid wheels, lower their titles of honor.

sentences.zh: 馳禽荒色，長違清編，嗜音酣酒，守官不徙。

translations.literal: Racing after birds and lost in lewd color, long breaking the pure statutes; addicted to music and drowned in wine, holding office without moving.
translations.idiomatic: Chasing birds and lost in lewd color, long outside the pure code; drunk on music and wine, holding office without moving.

sentences.zh: 物識義方，且懼且勸，則調風變俗，不俟終日。」

translations.literal: When things know the rule of right conduct, fearing yet urging—then to tune the wind and alter custom needs not wait a full day.」
translations.idiomatic: When things know duty and method, both fearing and urging—then to tune the wind and change custom need not wait a full day.」

sentences.zh: :　　又曰：「憲律之重，由來尚矣。

translations.literal: : Also he said: 「The weight of statutes and penalties has been honored from of old.
translations.idiomatic: Also he said: 「The weight of statutes and penalties has been honored from of old.

sentences.zh: 故曹參去齊，唯以獄市爲寄，餘無所言。

translations.literal: Therefore when Cao Shen left Qi he charged only the prisons and markets, and said nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore when Cao Shen left Qi he charged only the prisons and markets and said nothing else.

sentences.zh: 路溫舒言『秦有十失，其一尚在，治獄之吏是也』。

translations.literal: Lu Wenshu said, 『The Qin had ten failures; one remains today—the officers who judge prisons are it.』
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wenshu said, 『The Qin had ten failures; one remains today—the officers who judge prisons are it.』

sentences.zh: 寔宜清置廷尉，茂簡三官，寺丞獄主，彌重其選，研習律令，刪除繁苛。

translations.literal: Truly one should clearly appoint the Court Commandant, abundantly select the three offices, and for prison clerks and wardens weigh their selection all the more; study legal codes and delete redundant harshness.
translations.idiomatic: The Court Commandant should be appointed clearly and the three judicial offices staffed with care; prison clerks and wardens must be chosen with still greater rigor, trained in the codes, and relieved of redundant severity.

sentences.zh: 詔獄及兩縣，一月三訊，觀貌察情，欺枉必達。

translations.literal: For imperial prison cases and the two metropolitan counties, three interrogations a month; observe the face and probe the heart—deceit and injustice must be reached.
translations.idiomatic: For imperial prison cases and the two capital counties, hold three hearings a month; read face and spirit until fraud and wrong are exposed.

sentences.zh: 使明慎用刑，無忝大《易》，寧失不經，靡愧《周書》。

translations.literal: Enable enlightened, careful use of punishments, not failing the great Changes; better to miss than to punish without cause, without shame to the Documents of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Let punishments be applied with sober care, in keeping with the Great Changes—better to acquit wrongly than to convict wrongly, and without shame to the Documents of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 漢來治律有家，子孫竝世其業，聚徒講授，至數百人。

translations.literal: Since Han there were households that mastered law; sons and grandsons together inherited the profession generation upon generation; they gathered disciples to lecture, reaching several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, legal learning ran in families whose sons and grandsons carried the trade from age to age, gathering pupils until lecture halls held hundreds.

sentences.zh: 故張、于二氏，絜譽文、宣之世；

translations.literal: Thus the two houses Zhang and Yu won unstained fame in the Wen and Xuan reigns;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang and Yu clans won unstained fame under Emperors Wen and Xuan;

sentences.zh: 陳、郭兩族，流稱武、明之朝。

translations.literal: the two lineages Chen and Guo flowed in renown through the Wu and Ming courts.
translations.idiomatic: the Chen and Guo lines were praised through the reigns of Wu and Ming.

sentences.zh: 決獄無冤，慶昌枝裔，槐羇相襲，蟬紫傳輝。

translations.literal: They judged cases without wrongful convictions; their descendants flourished in glory; office after office like parasol and bridle passed down, rank emblems of cicada and purple robe handing on their splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Cases left their courts without a false verdict, and their lines prospered—high office breeding high office, purple and cicada insignia passed from father to son.

sentences.zh: 今廷尉律生，乃令史門戶，族非咸、弘，庭缺于訓。

translations.literal: Today the law students of the Court Commandant are merely clerk households; their families are not those of Xian and Hong; the court lacks the Yu clan's training.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Court Commandant's law trainees are little more than clerk families—no lineages like Xian or Hong, no court schooled as the Yu once schooled it.

sentences.zh: 刑之不措，抑此之由。

translations.literal: That punishments are not properly applied—this is the reason.
translations.idiomatic: That punishments misfire is largely why.

sentences.zh: 如詳擇篤厚之士，使習律令，試簡有徵，擢爲廷尉僚屬。

translations.literal: If sincere, solid men were carefully chosen, made to study legal codes, tested and screened for proof of ability, and promoted as Court Commandant aides—
translations.idiomatic: Choose men of solid character, train them in the statutes, test them for real aptitude, and raise the proven to posts under the Court Commandant—

sentences.zh: 苟官世其家而不美其績，鮮矣；

translations.literal: if offices were hereditary in the family yet their merit were not made beautiful, it would be rare;
translations.idiomatic: hereditary office without matching merit would be rare;

sentences.zh: 廢其職而欲善其事，未之有也。

translations.literal: abolish their craft and yet wish to do the work well—never has there been such.
translations.idiomatic: but abolish the craft and still expect mastery—when has that ever worked?

sentences.zh: 若劉累傳守其業，庖人不乏龍肝之饌，斷可知矣。」

translations.literal: As Liu Lei handed down his trade and cooks were never short of dragon-liver feasts, that may be decided with certainty.」
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Lei kept his art alive, kitchens never lacked dragon's liver—the precedent is plain.」

sentences.zh: :　　又曰：「樂者動天地，感鬼神，正情性，立人倫，其義大矣。

translations.literal: Again he said: 「Music moves heaven and earth, touches ghosts and spirits, rectifies disposition and nature, establishes human relations—its meaning is vast.
translations.idiomatic: Again he said: 「Music stirs heaven and earth, moves ghost and spirit, straightens feeling and nature, and sets human relations in order—its weight is immense.

sentences.zh: 桉前漢編戶千萬，太樂伶官方八百二十九人，孔光等奏罷不合經法者四百四十一人，正樂定員，唯置三百八十八人。

translations.literal: According to Former Han with registered households in the tens of millions, Grand Music officials numbered eight hundred twenty-nine; Kong Guang and others memorialized to dismiss those not conforming to canonical law, four hundred forty-one persons; rectified music fixed quota, only placed three hundred eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Former Han counted ten million households yet staffed the Grand Music office with 829 performers; Kong Guang and his colleagues proposed dismissing 441 who violated classical norms, fixing the establishment at 388.

sentences.zh: 今戶口不能百萬，而太樂雅、鄭，元徽時校試千有餘人，後堂雜伎，不在其數，糜廢力役，傷敗風俗。

translations.literal: Today households cannot reach a million, yet Grand Music—for elegant and popular styles—at the Yuanhui era examination tested over a thousand; rear-hall miscellaneous performers are not in the count; waste of labor and corvée injures custom.
translations.idiomatic: Our registers fall short of a million, yet Grand Music—court and popular alike—tested more than a thousand musicians in the Yuanhui reign, and the rear-hall troupes stand outside even that figure, wasting labor and corroding custom.

sentences.zh: 今欲撥邪歸道，莫若罷雜伎，王庭唯置鍾虡、羽戚、登歌而已。

translations.literal: Now wishing to turn away evil and return to the Way, none is better than dismissing miscellaneous performers; the royal court should only place bells and stones, feather-shield dancers, and ascent hymns.
translations.idiomatic: To steer away from decadence, dismiss the variety acts; let the royal court keep only bells and lithophones, shield-dancers, and the ascent hymns.

sentences.zh: 如此，則官充給養，國反淳風矣。」

translations.literal: Thus offices would be abundantly supplied, and the state would return to pure custom.」
translations.idiomatic: Then the ministry would be fed within its means and the realm would recover an honest wind.」

sentences.zh: :　　又曰：「論儒者以德化爲本；

translations.literal: Again he said: 「Those who discourse in Confucian terms take moral transformation as root;
translations.idiomatic: Again he said: 「Confucians take moral transformation as their root;

sentences.zh: 談法者以刻削爲體。

translations.literal: those who speak of law take harsh cutting as substance.
translations.idiomatic: legalists take harsh cutting as their substance.

sentences.zh: 道教治世之粱肉，刑憲亂世之藥石，故以教化比雨露，名法方風霜。

translations.literal: Dao teaching is grain and meat for governing the age; penal statutes are medicine for chaotic ages; thus compare teaching and transforming to rain and dew, name and law to wind and frost.
translations.idiomatic: The Way is grain and meat for a well-governed age; penal codes are medicine for a troubled one—hence teaching is likened to rain and dew, statute to wind and frost.

sentences.zh: 是以有恥且格，敬讓之樞紐；

translations.literal: Thus having shame and being corrected is the pivot of reverence and yielding;
translations.idiomatic: Shame that reforms conduct is the hinge of reverence and yielding;

sentences.zh: 令行禁止，爲國之關楗。

translations.literal: orders executed and prohibitions enforced is the gate-bar of the state.
translations.idiomatic: commands enforced and bans upheld are the gate-bar of the state.

sentences.zh: 然則天下治者，賞罰而已矣。

translations.literal: Thus for those who govern all under heaven, reward and punishment alone suffice.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, to govern the realm is to balance reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 賞不事豐，所病於不均；

translations.literal: In rewards, abundance is not the point—the ailment lies in unfairness;
translations.idiomatic: Rewards need not be lavish; the harm lies in unfairness;

sentences.zh: 罰不在重，所困於不當。

translations.literal: in punishments, severity is not the point—the distress lies in inappropriateness.
translations.idiomatic: punishments need not be heavy; the trouble lies in misapplication.

sentences.zh: 如令甲勳少，乙功多，賞甲而捨乙，天下必有不勸矣；

translations.literal: If A's merit is few and B's achievement many, yet you reward A and abandon B, all under heaven will surely cease to strive;
translations.idiomatic: If A merits little and B merits much, yet you honor A and pass over B, the empire will cease to strive;

sentences.zh: 丙罪重，丁眚輕，罰丁而赦丙，天下必有不悛矣。

translations.literal: if C's crime is heavy and D's offense light, yet you punish D and pardon C, all under heaven will surely cease to reform.
translations.idiomatic: if C's guilt is grave and D's slight, yet you punish D and spare C, the empire will cease to mend its ways.

sentences.zh: 是賞罰空行，無當乎勸沮。

translations.literal: Then reward and punishment run empty, not fitting encouragement and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments would run hollow, fit neither to reward nor to warn.

sentences.zh: 將令見罰者寵習之臣，受賞者仇讎之士，戮一人而萬國懼，賞匹夫而四海悅。」

translations.literal: Make those who see punishment favored, habitual ministers; those who receive reward, enemy foes; slay one man and ten thousand states fear; reward one commoner and the four seas rejoice.」
translations.idiomatic: Let those punished be pampered favorites, and those rewarded be sworn foes; kill one man and every state trembles, reward one commoner and the four seas rejoice.」

sentences.zh: :　　又曰：「籍稅以厚國，國虛民貧；

translations.literal: Again he said: 「Register taxes to fatten the state—the state grows hollow while the people grow poor;
translations.idiomatic: Again he said: 「Tax registers to fatten the treasury hollow the state and beggar the people;

sentences.zh: 廣田以實廩，國富民贍。

translations.literal: broaden fields to fill granaries—the state grows rich while the people are provided for.
translations.idiomatic: broad fields to fill granaries enrich the state and feed the people.

sentences.zh: 堯資用天之儲，實拯懷山之數。

translations.literal: Yao drew on heaven's storehouses, truly redeeming the count of mountains embraced by flood.
translations.idiomatic: Yao drew on heaven's granaries and truly rescued the tale of mountains drowned in flood.

sentences.zh: 湯憑分地之積，以勝流金之運。

translations.literal: Tang relied on the accumulation of divided fields to overcome the fortune of flowing metal.
translations.idiomatic: Tang built on the yield of allotted fields and overcame the age of flowing metal.

sentences.zh: 近代魏置典農，而中都足食；

translations.literal: In recent times Wei established chief-agriculture offices, and the central capital had enough food;
translations.idiomatic: In recent times Wei set up agrarian offices and the central capital ate its fill;

sentences.zh: 晉開汝、潁，而汴河委儲。

translations.literal: Jin opened Ru and Ying, and the Bian River piled with stores.
translations.idiomatic: Jin opened the Ru and Ying tracts and the Bian channel brimmed with grain.

sentences.zh: 今將掃辟咸、華，題鏤龍漠，宜簡役敦農，開田廣稼。

translations.literal: Now about to sweep and clear Xian and Hua, inscribe the Dragon Desert, one should simplify corvée and encourage farming, open fields and broaden crops.
translations.idiomatic: As we aim to sweep the heartland and mark the northern frontier, we should lighten corvée, urge farming, open land, and widen the harvest.

sentences.zh: 時罷山池之威禁，深抑豪右之兼擅，則兵民優贍，可以出師。」

translations.literal: For now abolish the harsh prohibitions on mountain pools, deeply restrain great clans' monopolies—then soldiers and people will be well provided and armies may march.」
translations.idiomatic: Lift the ban on mountain and pond revenues, curb great-house encroachment, and troops and people alike will be ample enough to take the field.」

sentences.zh: :　　又曰：「古者左史記言，右史記事，故君舉必書，盡直筆而不污；

translations.literal: Again he said: 「Anciently the left historian recorded words and the right historian recorded affairs; thus the ruler's every act was written, the straight brush fully used without stain;
translations.idiomatic: Again he said: 「Of old the left scribe recorded words and the right scribe recorded deeds, so every act of the ruler was entered, brush straight and unstained;

sentences.zh: 上無妄動，知如絲之成綸。

translations.literal: the superior had no rash movements, knowing as silk threads form a cord.
translations.idiomatic: the lord made no rash move, knowing that threads become a cable.

sentences.zh: 今者著作之官，起居而已；

translations.literal: Today the compilation-office officials merely rise and retire;
translations.idiomatic: Today the compilers note who rose and who retired;

sentences.zh: 述事之徒，褒諛爲體。

translations.literal: those who narrate affairs take flattery as substance.
translations.idiomatic: those who recount events traffic in praise.

sentences.zh: 世無董狐，書法必隱；

translations.literal: An age without Dong Hu—the writing law must hide;
translations.idiomatic: Without a Dong Hu, the law of record must hide the truth;

sentences.zh: 時闕南史，直筆未聞。」

translations.literal: a time lacking the Southern Historian—the straight brush is unheard.」
translations.idiomatic: without a Southern Scribe, the straight brush is nowhere heard.」

sentences.zh: :　　又曰：「廢諫官，則聽納靡依。

translations.literal: Again he said: 「If remonstrance officials are abolished, listening and accepting have no support.
translations.idiomatic: Again he said: 「Abolish remonstrance officers and the throne has nothing firm to lean on.

sentences.zh: 雖課勵朝僚，徵訪芻輿，莫若推舉質直，職思其憂。

translations.literal: Though one urges court colleagues and seeks grass-cart opinion, none is better than recommending sincere, upright men who in office ponder its cares.
translations.idiomatic: Lecturing courtiers or polling rural opinion cannot match raising blunt, honest men who take their charge to heart.

sentences.zh: 夫越任于事，在言爲難；

translations.literal: To overstep one's charge in affairs—in speech it is hard;
translations.idiomatic: To speak beyond one's brief is hard;

sentences.zh: 當官而行，處辭或易。

translations.literal: to act in office—in handling words it is perhaps easy.
translations.idiomatic: to act from office is often easier on the tongue.

sentences.zh: 物議旣以無言望己，己亦當以吞默慚人。

translations.literal: Public opinion already expects silence of oneself; oneself should also be ashamed before others in swallowing silence.
translations.idiomatic: The world already expects your silence; you should be ashamed to grant it.

sentences.zh: 中丞雖謝咸、玄，未有全廢劾簡；

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief may have declined Xian and Xuan, but impeachment memoranda have not been wholly abolished;
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief may have set aside Xian and Xuan, yet the power to impeach has not been cast off entirely;

sentences.zh: 廷尉誠非釋之，寧容都無訊牒。

translations.literal: The Director of Justice is no Zhang Shizhi—yet how can there be no interrogation papers at all?
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Justice is no Zhang Shizhi—yet how can the docket stand utterly empty?

sentences.zh: 故知與其謬人，寧不廢職，目前之明效也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows: better to employ the wrong man than abolish the office—a lesson plain before one's eyes.
translations.idiomatic: The lesson is clear: keep the post filled, even with the wrong man, rather than abolish it—a truth the present age proves.

sentences.zh: 漢徵貢禹爲諫大夫，矢言先策，夏侯勝狂直拘繫，出補諷職，伐柯非遐，行之卽善。」

translations.literal: Under Han, Gong Yu was summoned as Remonstrance Grandee and spoke first of policy; Xia Hou Sheng, wildly upright, was imprisoned, then sent out to fill a satire post—cutting the handle is not far off; do it and the good follows at once.」
translations.idiomatic: Under Han, Gong Yu was called up as Remonstrance Grandee and set policy first; Xia Hou Sheng, blunt to the point of madness, was bound, then sent out to a post of mockery—yet the handle is near at hand to cut; act, and the good comes at once.」

sentences.zh: :　　又曰：「天地無心，賦氣自均，寧得誕秀往古，而獨寂寥一代，將在知與不知，用與不用耳。

translations.literal: : He also said: 「Heaven and earth have no mind; vital force distributes itself evenly. How could gifted men appear only in antiquity while this age alone stands empty? It lies in knowing or not knowing, employing or not employing.」
translations.idiomatic: He said again: 「Heaven and earth bear no intent; breath is allotted evenly. How could excellence be born only in the past, while our age alone stands bare? The difference is knowing or not knowing, using or not using.」

sentences.zh: 夫有賢而不知，知賢而不用，用賢而不委，委賢而不信，此四者，古今之通患也。

translations.literal: To have worthies and not know them, to know worthies and not use them, to use worthies and not entrust them, to entrust worthies and not trust them—these four are the common afflictions of every age.
translations.idiomatic: Worthies present but unknown; known but not used; used but not empowered; empowered but not trusted—these four have been the standing grief of every age.

sentences.zh: 今誠重郭隗而招劇辛，任鮑叔以求夷吾，則天下之士，不待召而自至矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would truly honor Guo Wei to draw Ju Xin, and trust Bao Shuya to seek Guan Zhong, then men of talent throughout the realm would come without waiting to be summoned.」
translations.idiomatic: Honor Guo Wei as Yan did, and Ju Xin will come; trust Bao Shuya as Duke Huan did, and Guan Zhong will be found—then the realm's worthies will arrive without a summons.」

sentences.zh: 上優詔報答。

translations.literal: The emperor replied with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: The throne answered with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 尋遷寧朔將軍、冠軍司馬，領齊郡太守、本官如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to General Who Pacifies the North, champion chief clerk, and administrator of Qi commandery, his other posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was named General Who Pacifies the North and champion chief clerk, with Qi commandery added to his charge; his other offices stood as before.

sentences.zh: 是冬，虜動，遷冠軍將軍、軍主，屯淮上。

translations.literal: That winter the northerners stirred. He was transferred to Champion General and army commander, and camped on the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the northerners moved. He was shifted to Champion General and army commander and posted on the Huai.

sentences.zh: 二年，進號征虜將軍，軍主如故。

translations.literal: In the second year his title advanced to General Who Punishes the Barbarians; his command of the army was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was raised to General Who Punishes the Barbarians, still commanding the army as before.

sentences.zh: 仍遷假節、督青冀二州刺史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was then given acting credentials and made overseer of the two provinces Qing and Ji; his general's rank stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was then granted acting credentials and put in charge of Qing and Ji; his general's rank was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 少時，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, he died.

sentences.zh: 上歎曰：「我方欲用祖思，不幸，可惜。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said: 「I was only just about to employ Zusi—this is ill fortune, and a pity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said: 「I had only just begun to rely on Zusi—what ill luck. A waste.

sentences.zh: 」詔賻錢三萬，布五十匹。

translations.literal: 」An edict granted thirty thousand cash for funeral expenses and fifty bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: 」An edict granted thirty thousand in funeral cash and fifty bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 祖思宗人文仲，初辟州從事。

translations.literal: Zusi's clansman Wen Zhong was first recruited as a provincial staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Zusi's kinsman Wen Zhong was first taken on as a provincial staff officer.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，爲薛安都平北主簿，拔難歸國。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he served as chief clerk under Xue Andu's Pacify-the-North headquarters; he escaped hardship and returned to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taishi he was chief clerk on Xue Andu's Pacify-the-North staff; he broke through danger and came back to the south.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，從太祖於新亭拒桂陽賊，著誠效，除游擊將軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanhui he followed the Grand Ancestor at Xinting in resisting the Guiyang rebels, gave proof of loyalty, and was made Mobile-Strike General.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanhui he followed the Grand Ancestor to Xinting against the Guiyang rebels, proved his loyalty, and was made Mobile-Strike General.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，助豫章王鎮東府，歷驃騎諮議，出爲徐州刺史。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair broke out, he aided the Prince of Yuzhang in garrisoning the Eastern Palace, served as consultative officer of the Rapid Cavalry, and went out as inspector of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rose, he helped the Prince of Yuzhang hold the Eastern Palace, served as Rapid Cavalry consultative officer, and went out as inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 建元初，封建陽縣子，三百戶。

translations.literal: At the opening of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as village Marquis of Yangcheng, with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Jianyuan he was made village Marquis of Yangcheng, with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 二年，虜攻鍾離，仲文擊破之。

translations.literal: In the second year the northerners attacked Zhongli; Wen Zhong routed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the northerners pressed Zhongli; Wen Zhong beat them back.

sentences.zh: 又遣軍主崔孝伯等過淮攻拔虜茬眉戍，殺戍主龍得侯及偽陽平太守郭杜羝，館陶令張德，濮陽令王明。

translations.literal: He also sent the army commander Cui Xiaobo and others across the Huai to storm and take the northerners' Chamazhi garrison, killing the garrison chief Long Dehou, the puppet administrator of Yangping Guo Durong, the magistrate of Guantao Zhang De, and the magistrate of Puyang Wang Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent army commander Cui Xiaobo and others across the Huai to storm the northerners' Chamazhi fort, killing the garrison chief Long Dehou, the puppet Yangping administrator Guo Durong, Guantao magistrate Zhang De, and Puyang magistrate Wang Ming.

sentences.zh: 時虜攻殺馬頭太守劉從，上曰：「破茬眉，足相補。

translations.literal: At that time the northerners attacked and killed the administrator of Matou, Liu Cong. The emperor said: 「Taking Chamazhi makes up for that well enough.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the northerners attacked and killed Liu Cong, administrator of Matou. The emperor said: 「Breaking Chamazhi balances the ledger well enough.

sentences.zh: 」文仲又遣軍主陳靖攻虜竹邑戍主白仲都，又遣軍主崔延叔攻偽淮陽太守梁惡，竝殺之。

translations.literal: 」Wen Zhong again sent the army commander Chen Jing to attack the northerners' garrison chief at Zhuyi, Bai Zhongdu, and sent the army commander Cui Yanshu to attack the puppet administrator of Huaiyang, Liang E—and killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: 」Wen Zhong sent army commander Chen Jing against the Zhuyi garrison chief Bai Zhongdu, and army commander Cui Yanshu against the puppet Huaiyang administrator Liang E—and killed them both.

sentences.zh: 三年，淮北義民桓磊磈於抱犢固與虜戰，大破之。

translations.literal: In the third year the righteous commoner of Huaibei, Huan Leikai, fought the northerners at Baodugu and broke them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Huan Leikai, a righteous man of Huaibei, fought the northerners at Baodugu and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 仲文馳啓，上敕曰：「北閒起義者衆，深恐良會不再至，卿善獎沛中人，若能一時攘袂，當遣一佳將直入也。

translations.literal: Wen Zhong sent an urgent memorial; the emperor commanded: 「Uprisings north of the border are many, and I deeply fear this good moment may not come again. Encourage the men of Pei well—if they can roll up their sleeves at once, I shall send in an excellent general straight through.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhong sent an urgent report; the emperor commanded: 「The north is full of rising loyalists, and I fear this ripe hour may not return. Stir the men of Pei—if they will roll up their sleeves together, I shall send a first-rate general straight in.

sentences.zh: 」文仲在政，爲百姓所憚。

translations.literal: 」Wen Zhong's government struck the common people with awe.
translations.idiomatic: 」In office, Wen Zhong was a man the common people feared.

sentences.zh: 除黃門郎，領越騎校尉，改封隨縣。

translations.literal: He was made Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, with the added post of Colonel of Rapid Cavalry, and his fief was changed to Sui county.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, with the added post of Colonel of Rapid Cavalry, and his fief was moved to Sui county.

sentences.zh: 嘗獻太祖纏鬚繩一枚，上爲納受。

translations.literal: Once he presented the Grand Ancestor with a coil of beard-binding cord; the throne accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Once he offered the Grand Ancestor a coil of beard-binding cord, and the throne took it.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，爲太子左率，累至征虜將軍、冠軍司馬、汝陰太守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming he was Left Leader of the Crown Prince's Household, and rose in stages to General Who Punishes the Barbarians, champion chief clerk, and administrator of Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming 1 he was Left Leader of the Crown Prince's Household, and in time rose to General Who Punishes the Barbarians, champion chief clerk, and administrator of Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died.

sentences.zh: 贈後將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Rear General and inspector of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: After death he was given Rear General and inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 諡襄子。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Xiangzi.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Xiangzi.

sentences.zh: 劉善明

translations.literal: Liu Shanming
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shanming

sentences.zh: 劉善明，平原人。

translations.literal: Liu Shanming was a man of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shanming came from Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍懷珍族弟也。

translations.literal: He was a younger cousin of Liu Huaizhen, General Who Guards the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was a younger cousin of Liu Huaizhen, General Who Guards the North.

sentences.zh: 父懷民，宋世爲齊北海二郡太守。

translations.literal: His father Huaimin had served in the Song as administrator of the two commanderies Qi and Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huaimin had governed Qi and Beihai under the Song.

sentences.zh: 元嘉末，青州飢荒，人相食，善明家有積粟，躬食饘粥，開倉以救郷里，多獲全濟，百姓呼其家田爲「續命田」。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia, Qingzhou was in famine and men ate one another. Shanming's household had grain laid by; he ate thin gruel himself and opened his granary to save the neighborhood. Many were brought through alive, and the people called his family's fields the Fields That Gave Life Back.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanjia, Qingzhou starved until men ate one another. Shanming's family had grain in store; he lived on thin gruel himself and opened the bins to save the neighborhood. Many lived who would have died, and the people called his family's fields the Fields That Gave Life Back.

sentences.zh: 少而靜處讀書，刺史杜驥聞名候之，辭不相見。

translations.literal: In youth he sat quietly and read; the inspector Du Ji, hearing his fame, came to call on him, but Shanming declined to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he read in seclusion; Inspector Du Ji, hearing his name, came to call, but Shanming would not see him.

sentences.zh: 年四十，刺史劉道隆辟爲治中從事。

translations.literal: At forty the inspector Liu Daolong recruited him as chief clerk of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At forty, Inspector Liu Daolong took him on as headquarters chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 父懷民謂善明曰：「我已知汝立身，復欲見汝立官也。

translations.literal: His father Huaimin said to Shanming: 「I already know how you will stand as a man; I wish now to see how you will stand in office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huaimin told him: 「I already know the man you will be; I want now to see the officer you will become.

sentences.zh: 」善明應辟。

translations.literal: 」Shanming accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: 」Shanming accepted the post.

sentences.zh: 仍舉秀才。

translations.literal: He was also nominated as Promoted Talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was also nominated as Promoted Talent.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武見其對策強直，甚異之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song read his examination answers and found them forcefully direct; he was greatly struck.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Song read his examination answers—blunt and unyielding—and marveled at them.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，徐州刺史薛安都反，青州刺史沈文秀應之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, Xue Andu, inspector of Xu, rebelled, and Shen Wenxiu of Qing responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taishi, Xue Andu, inspector of Xu, rebelled, and Shen Wenxiu of Qing rose with him.

sentences.zh: 時州治東陽城，善明家在郭內，不能自拔。

translations.literal: The provincial seat was then at Dongyang city; Shanming's family lay inside the suburbs and could not break free.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial seat was at Dongyang; Shanming's household was inside the wall and could not escape.

sentences.zh: 伯父彌之詭說文秀求自效，文秀使領軍主張靈慶等五千援安都。

translations.literal: His uncle Mizhi deceived Wenxiu with a plea to prove himself; Wenxiu sent the army commander Zhang Lingqing and five thousand men to aid Andu.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Mizhi tricked Wenxiu into trusting him to prove his worth; Wenxiu sent army commander Zhang Lingqing with five thousand men to aid Andu.

sentences.zh: 彌之出門，密謂部曲曰：「始免禍坑矣。

translations.literal: When Mizhi passed the gate he whispered to his retainers: 「At last we are out of the pit of ruin.
translations.idiomatic: As Mizhi left the gate he whispered to his men: 「At last we have climbed out of the pit.

sentences.zh: 」行至下邳，起義背文秀。

translations.literal: 」At Xiapi he rose in loyalty and turned against Wenxiu.
translations.idiomatic: 」At Xiapi he rose for the throne and turned on Wenxiu.

sentences.zh: 善明從伯懷恭爲北海太守，據郡相應。

translations.literal: Shanming's elder cousin Huaimin held Beihai as administrator and kept the commandery in answer to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Shanming's elder cousin Huaimin was administrator of Beihai and held the commandery for the court.

sentences.zh: 善明密契收集門宗部曲，得三千人，夜斬關奔北海。

translations.literal: Shanming secretly made compact with his clan, gathered its retainers, mustered three thousand men, and by night cut through the gate and fled to Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Shanming bound his clan in secret, rallied its household troops to three thousand, and in the dark broke the gate and ran for Beihai.

sentences.zh: 族兄乘民又聚衆渤海以應朝廷。

translations.literal: His kinsman Chengmin also raised a host in Bohai to answer the court.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Chengmin likewise gathered men in Bohai to declare for the throne.

sentences.zh: 而彌之尋爲薛安都所殺，明帝贈輔國將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long Mizhi was killed by Xue Andu; Emperor Ming posthumously made him general who supports the state and inspector of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhi was soon slain by Xue Andu; Emperor Ming ennobled him posthumously as general who supports the state and inspector of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以乘民爲寧朔將軍、冀州刺史，善明爲寧朔長史、北海太守，除尚書金部郎。

translations.literal: Chengmin was made general who calms the north and inspector of Jizhou; Shanming was made chief aide to the general who calms the north and administrator of Beihai, and also appointed director of the ministry of revenue's gold bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Chengmin became general who calms the north and inspector of Jizhou; Shanming took chief aide and administrator of Beihai under that command, and was named director of the ministry of revenue's gold bureau.

sentences.zh: 乘民病卒，仍以善明爲綏遠將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Chengmin died of illness; Shanming was still made general who comforts the distant and inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengmin died in office, Shanming was left in his place as general who comforts the distant and inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 文秀旣降，除善明爲屯騎校尉，出爲海陵太守。

translations.literal: Once Wenshu had surrendered, Shanming was made commandant of the reserve cavalry and sent out as administrator of Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenshu came in, Shanming was named commandant of the reserve cavalry and posted as administrator of Hailing.

sentences.zh: 郡境邊海，無樹木，善明課民種榆檟雜果，遂獲其利。

translations.literal: The commandery bordered the sea and had no trees; Shanming ordered the people to plant elms, catalpas, and mixed fruit, and they soon profited by it.
translations.idiomatic: The coast had no timber; Shanming set the people to planting elms, catalpas, and orchard trees, and the district soon thrived on the harvest.

sentences.zh: 還爲後軍將軍、直閤。

translations.literal: He returned to be rear guard general and director of the inner gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as rear guard general and director of the inner gate.

sentences.zh: 五年，青州沒虜，善明母陷北，虜移置桑乾。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Qingzhou fell to the barbarians; Shanming's mother was taken north, and the barbarians resettled her at Sanggan.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 Qingzhou was lost to the northerners; Shanming's mother was carried off and settled at Sanggan.

sentences.zh: 善明布衣蔬食，哀戚如持喪。

translations.literal: Shanming wore plain cloth and ate coarse food, grieving as though in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Shanming dressed in hemp and ate sparingly, mourning her as though she were already dead.

sentences.zh: 明帝每見，爲之歎息，時人稱之。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Ming saw him he sighed for him; men of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Emperor Ming received him he sighed with pity; contemporaries spoke of his devotion.

sentences.zh: 轉寧朔將軍、巴西梓潼二郡太守。

translations.literal: He was moved to general who calms the north and administrator of the two commanderies Brazil and Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to general who calms the north and administrator of Brazil and Zitong.

sentences.zh: 善明以母在虜中，不願西行，涕泣固請，見許。

translations.literal: Because his mother was among the barbarians, Shanming would not go west; weeping, he begged firmly and was allowed.
translations.idiomatic: With his mother still in the north, Shanming refused the western post; he pleaded with tears until the court relented.

sentences.zh: 朝廷多哀善明心事。

translations.literal: The court widely pitied Shanming's heartfelt plight.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court pitied the bond that held him back.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，遣北使，朝議令善明舉人，善明舉州郷北平田惠紹使虜，贖得母還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui an envoy was sent north; court discussion had Shanming nominate a man; Shanming nominated his fellow townsman Tian Huishaokuo of Beiping to go to the barbarians and ransom his mother home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhui the court sent a northern envoy and asked Shanming to name a man; he put forward his townsman Tian Huishaokuo of Beiping, who crossed to the barbarians and bought his mother back.

sentences.zh: 幼主新立，羣公秉政，善明獨結事太祖，委身歸誠。

translations.literal: The young emperor had just taken the throne; the great lords held power; Shanming alone attached himself to the Grand Ancestor and gave himself over in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When the boy emperor mounted the throne and the great families ruled, Shanming alone threw in his lot with the Grand Ancestor and pledged himself without reserve.

sentences.zh: 二年，出爲輔國將軍、西海太守、行青冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he went out as general who supports the state, administrator of Xihai, and acting inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he took the field as general who supports the state, administrator of Xihai, and acting inspector of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，表請北伐，朝議不同。

translations.literal: On reaching his post he memorialized asking for a northern campaign; court opinion did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: At his post he asked leave to march north; the court would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 善明從弟僧副，與善明俱知名於州里。

translations.literal: Shanming's younger cousin Sengfu was, with Shanming, famed in their province.
translations.idiomatic: Shanming's cousin Sengfu shared his name throughout the province.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，虜暴淮北，僧副將部曲二千人東依海島，太祖在淮陰，壯其所爲，召與相見，引爲安成王撫軍參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi the barbarians ravaged north of the Huai; Sengfu led two thousand retainers east to island refuges along the coast; the Grand Ancestor was at Huaiyin, admired his conduct, summoned him for an audience, and took him on as staff officer to the Prince of Ancheng's pacifying army.
translations.idiomatic: When Taishi opened, the northerners swept the Huai north; Sengfu took two thousand household troops to coastal islands. The Grand Ancestor, then at Huaiyin, admired his nerve, called him in, and made him a staff officer on Prince Ancheng's pacifying army.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧肆暴，太祖憂恐，常令僧副微行伺察聲論。

translations.literal: Cangwu ran wild with cruelty; the Grand Ancestor was pressed with worry and fear; he often had Sengfu go in disguise to listen to public talk.
translations.idiomatic: Cangwu's cruelty ran unchecked and the Grand Ancestor lived in dread; he often sent Sengfu out in plain dress to catch the mood of the streets.

sentences.zh: 使僧副密告善明及東海太守垣崇祖曰：「多人見勸北固廣陵，恐一旦動足，非爲長算。

translations.literal: He had Sengfu secretly tell Shanming and the administrator of Donghai, Yuan Chongzu, saying: 「Many urge me to move on Beigu and Guangling; I fear that if I stir once, it will not be a lasting plan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Sengfu to tell Shanming and Yuan Chongzu, administrator of Donghai, in secret: 「Many counsel me to seize Beigu and Guangling, but one rash move would not be a lasting plan.

sentences.zh: 今秋風行起，卿若能與垣東海微共動虜，則我諸計可立。

translations.literal: Now the autumn wind is rising; if you can lightly stir the barbarians together with Lord Yuan of Donghai, then all my designs can stand.」
translations.idiomatic: The autumn wind is rising. If you and Lord Yuan of Donghai can nudge the barbarians into motion, every scheme I have laid will take hold.」

sentences.zh: 」善明曰：「宋氏將亡，愚智所辨。

translations.literal: 」Shanming said: 「The house of Song is near its fall; fool and sage alike can tell.
translations.idiomatic: 」Shanming answered: 「Song's end is plain to fool and sage alike.

sentences.zh: 故胡虜若動，反爲公患。

translations.literal: Therefore if the northern barbarians stir, they will become trouble for you.
translations.idiomatic: Let the northern barbarians move, and they become your trouble, not your tool.

sentences.zh: 公神武世出，唯當靜以待之，因機奮發，功業自定。

translations.literal: My lord, your divine martial worth towers over the age; you have only to wait in stillness, then rise when the moment comes—your achievement will settle itself.
translations.idiomatic: Your martial genius stands above the age; wait in stillness, strike when heaven opens the way, and your work will finish itself.

sentences.zh: 不可遠去根本，自貽猖蹶。

translations.literal: You must not go far from your root and bring ruin on yourself.」
translations.idiomatic: Do not leave your base and court disaster.」

sentences.zh: 」遣部曲健兒數十人隨僧副還詣領府，太祖納之。

translations.literal: He sent several dozen stalwart retainers with Sengfu back to the command headquarters; the Grand Ancestor accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent several dozen picked men back with Sengfu to headquarters; the Grand Ancestor took them in.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧廢，徵善明爲冠軍將軍、太祖驃騎諮議、南東海太守、行南徐州事。

translations.literal: When Cangwu was deposed, Shanming was summoned as champion general, staff adviser to the Grand Ancestor's swift-cavalry command, administrator of South Donghai, and acting governor of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Cangwu was cast down, Shanming was called in as champion general, staff adviser to the Grand Ancestor's swift-cavalry command, administrator of South Donghai, and acting governor of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之反，太祖深以爲憂。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, the Grand Ancestor was deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi turned rebel, the Grand Ancestor was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 善明獻計曰：「沈攸之控引八州，縱情蓄歛，收衆聚騎，營造舟仗，苞藏賊志，於焉十年。

translations.literal: Shanming offered a plan, saying: 「Shen Youzhi draws on eight provinces, indulges his will in hoarding wealth, gathers soldiers and horses, builds boats and arms, and nurses treason in his heart—ten years of it.
translations.idiomatic: Shanming laid out a plan: 「Youzhi commands eight provinces, taxes as he pleases, herds men and horses, builds ships and weapons, and has nursed treason these ten years.

sentences.zh: 性旣險躁，才非持重，而起逆累旬，遲回不進。

translations.literal: His nature is treacherous and rash; his talent is not weighty; yet he has raised rebellion for many tens of days and hangs back without advancing.
translations.idiomatic: He is treacherous and rash, not steady in counsel, yet weeks into rebellion he still will not close.

sentences.zh: 豈應有所待也？

translations.literal: Can he be waiting for something?
translations.idiomatic: What could he still be waiting for?

sentences.zh: 一則闇於兵機，二則人情離怨，三則有掣肘之患，四則天奪其魄。

translations.literal: First, he is blind to the art of war; second, hearts under him are estranged and resentful; third, he has the trouble of men who pull his elbows; fourth, heaven has stolen his soul.
translations.idiomatic: First, he does not grasp war; second, his men are divided and bitter; third, rivals tug at his sleeves; fourth, heaven has taken his nerve.

sentences.zh: 本慮其剽勇，長於一戰，疑其輕速，掩襲未備。

translations.literal: I had feared his fierce courage and his gift for a single pitched battle, and wondered whether he might strike fast and raid us unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: I feared his ferocity in a single clash and wondered if he might strike before we were ready.

sentences.zh: 今六師齊奮，諸侯同舉。

translations.literal: Now the six armies rise together and the feudal lords march as one.
translations.idiomatic: Now the six hosts advance as one and every lord has raised his banner.

sentences.zh: 昔謝晦失理，不鬬自潰；

translations.literal: In the past Xie Hui lost the right course and collapsed without fighting;
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui once lost the way and broke without a battle;

sentences.zh: 盧龍乖道，雖衆何施。

translations.literal: Lu Long went against the Way—what use were his masses?
translations.idiomatic: Lu Long defied heaven—of what use were his crowds?

sentences.zh: 且袁粲、劉秉，賊之根本，根本旣滅，枝葉豈久。

translations.literal: Moreover Yuan Can and Liu Bing are the root of the rebels; once the root is cut, can the branches last?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can and Liu Bing are the root of this revolt; cut the root and the branches cannot stand long.

sentences.zh: 此是已籠之鳥耳。

translations.literal: This is a bird already in the cage.」
translations.idiomatic: This is a bird already caged.」

sentences.zh: 」事平，太祖召善明還都，謂之曰：「卿策沈攸之，雖復張良、陳平，適如此耳。

translations.literal: 」When the affair was settled, the Grand Ancestor summoned Shanming back to the capital and told him: 「Your forecast on Shen Youzhi—even Zhang Liang and Chen Ping would have done no more.」
translations.idiomatic: 」When the war ended, the Grand Ancestor called Shanming home and said, 「Your reading of Shen Youzhi—Zhang Liang and Chen Ping could not have done better.」

sentences.zh: 」仍遷散騎常侍，領長水校尉，黃門郎，領後軍將軍、太尉右司馬。

translations.literal: He was then moved to attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered riders, with concurrent office as commandant of the long river, palace gate officer, and rear guard general with concurrent post as right aide to the grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was made attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered riders, commandant of the long river, palace gate officer, and rear guard general with concurrent post as right aide to the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 齊臺建，爲右衞將軍，辭疾不拜。

translations.literal: When the Qi platform was established, he was made right guard general but declined on grounds of illness and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regime was set up he was named right guard general but pleaded illness and would not take the seal.

sentences.zh: 司空褚淵謂善明曰：「高尚之事，乃卿從來素意。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chu Yuan said to Shanming: 「A life of lofty withdrawal has always been your wish.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan, minister of works, told him, 「Renouncing office for a lofty life has always been your bent.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷方相委待，詎得便學松、喬邪？

translations.literal: Now the court is about to lean on you—how can you suddenly take lessons from the pine and the catalpa?」
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court is ready to lean on you—will you play hermit among pines and catalpas now?」

sentences.zh: 」善明曰：「我本無宦情，旣逢知己，所以戮力驅馳，願在申志。

translations.literal: 」Shanming said: 「I never had appetite for office; having met a man who knew me, I drove myself on to repay him and hoped only to make my will plain.
translations.idiomatic: 」Shanming said, 「I never hungered for rank; once I met a lord who knew me, I strained every nerve to serve him and only wished to prove my heart.

sentences.zh: 今天地廓清，朝盈濟濟，鄙懷旣申，不敢昧於富貴矣。

translations.literal: Now heaven and earth are cleared, the court is full to overflowing; my humble wish has been answered—I dare not linger blind in wealth and honor.」
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm is settled and the court throngs with talent; my wish is fulfilled—I will not grope after riches and titles.」

sentences.zh: 」太祖踐阼，以善明勳誠，欲與善明祿，召謂之曰：「淮南近畿，國之形勢，自非親賢，不使居之。

translations.literal: 」When the Grand Ancestor took the throne, because of Shanming's merit and loyalty he wished to reward him with rank, summoned him, and said: 「Huainan lies on the near frontier; it is the shape of the realm. Unless a man is kin or proven worthy, he must not hold it.
translations.idiomatic: 」At the Grand Ancestor's accession he meant to honor Shanming's service, called him in, and said, 「Huainan borders the capital heartland; it is the hinge of the realm. Only kin or proven men should guard it.

sentences.zh: 卿爲我卧治也！

translations.literal: Govern it for me from your couch!」
translations.idiomatic: Rule it for me from your couch!」

sentences.zh: 」代高宗爲征虜將軍、淮南宣城二郡太守，遣使拜授，封新淦伯，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: 」He replaced Gao Zong as general who campaigns against barbarians and administrator of the two commanderies Huainan and Xuancheng; envoys were sent to invest him; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xingan with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: 」He took Gao Zong's place as general who campaigns against barbarians and administrator of Huainan and Xuancheng; envoys brought the commission; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xingan with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 善明至郡，上表陳事曰：「周以三聖相資，再駕乃就。

translations.literal: When Shanming reached the commandery, he memorialized the throne: 「Zhou relied on three sages in mutual aid before the second ascent to rule was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanming arrived in his province, he submitted a memorial: 「Zhou drew on three sage rulers in succession before the chariot of state could be driven a second time.

sentences.zh: 漢值海內無主，累敗方登。

translations.literal: When Han came, the realm within the seas had no master; only after repeated defeats did it ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Han rose when the realm had no lord, and the throne was won only after defeat upon defeat.

sentences.zh: 魏挾主行令，實踰二紀。

translations.literal: Wei held the emperor and issued orders; in truth it passed two reign cycles.
translations.idiomatic: Wei ruled in the emperor's name for more than two full reign cycles.

sentences.zh: 晉廢立持權，遂歷四世。

translations.literal: Jin deposed and enthroned while holding power; thus it ran through four generations.
translations.idiomatic: Jin kept power through deposition and enthronement, and so held sway for four generations.

sentences.zh: 景祚攸集，如此之難者也。

translations.literal: When the bright mandate gathers, the difficulty is as great as this.
translations.idiomatic: When fortune's light gathers, the climb is as hard as this.

sentences.zh: 陛下凝暉自天，照湛神極，睿周萬品，道洽無垠。

translations.literal: Your Majesty condenses radiance from Heaven, shines and sinks into the divine pole, wisdom encompasses the ten thousand kinds, and the Way reaches without bound.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty draws radiance from Heaven, floods the sacred pole with light, embraces the ten thousand kinds in wisdom, and extends the Way without limit.

sentences.zh: 故能高嘯閑軒，鯨鯢自翦，垂拱雲帟，九服載晏，靡一戰之勞，無半辰之棘，苞池江海，籠苑嵩岱，神祇樂推，普天歸奉，二三年閒，允膺寶命，冑臨皇曆，正位宸居，開闢以來，未有若斯之盛者也。

translations.literal: Therefore you can cry high from the idle hall; whales and krakens cut themselves down; bowing from the cloud canopy, the nine domains all rest in peace—with not one battle's toil, not half a watch's thorn, embracing pool, river, and sea, caging park, Song, and Mount Tai; spirits and gods gladly push, all under Heaven return in homage; within two or three years you truly received the precious mandate, donned the imperial succession, took the correct seat in the imperial dwelling—since the opening of the age, there has never been such splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Hence you may sing from a quiet hall while great foes cut themselves down; bowing beneath the cloud canopy, the nine domains rest in peace—without the labor of a single battle, without half a watch's anguish; seas and rivers lie within your pool, Song and Mount Tai within your park; spirits and gods press you forward, and all under Heaven returns in homage. In two or three years you truly received the precious mandate, took up the imperial succession, and sat the throne aright—since the world began, there has been no splendor like this.

sentences.zh: 夫常勝者無憂，恒成者好怠。

translations.literal: Those who always win have no worry; those who always succeed grow fond of slackness.
translations.idiomatic: Those who always win cease to worry; those who always succeed grow slack.

sentences.zh: 故雖休勿休，姬旦作誥；

translations.literal: Therefore though at rest, do not rest—the Duke of Zhou made the Announcements;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, though at rest, do not rest—the Duke of Zhou wrote his Announcements;

sentences.zh: 安不忘危，尼父垂範。

translations.literal: in security forget not danger—Confucius left the model.
translations.idiomatic: in security forget not danger—Confucius left his model.

sentences.zh: 今皇運草創，萬化始基，乘宋季葉，政多澆苛，億兆倒懸，仰齊蘇振。

translations.literal: Now the imperial fortune is newly founded and the ten thousand transformations begin their base; riding the late leaf of Song, government was mostly harsh and thin; the hundred millions hung inverted, looking up to Su's revival.
translations.idiomatic: Now the imperial fortune is newly forged and every transformation begins its footing; we rise from Song's late decline, when government ran harsh and thin; the people hung inverted, looking up for a revival like Su's.

sentences.zh: 臣早蒙殊養，志輸肝血，徒有其誠，曾闕埃露。

translations.literal: Your servant long received special nurture; his will poured out liver and blood—he had only sincerity, yet once lacked even dust and dew.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant was long nurtured with special favor; his heart poured out blood and liver—he had only sincerity, yet could not offer even dust or dew.

sentences.zh: 夙宵慚戰，如墜淵谷，不識忌諱，謹陳愚管，瞽言芻議，伏待斧鉞。

translations.literal: Morning and night he battles shame, as if falling into an abyss valley; not knowing taboo, he respectfully sets forth his foolish tube, blind words and hay counsel, prostrate awaiting the axe.
translations.idiomatic: Night and morning shame assails him, as though he were falling into an abyss; ignorant of taboo, he respectfully offers this foolish counsel—blind words, hay arguments—and lies prostrate awaiting the axe.

sentences.zh: 」所陳事凡十一條：其一，以爲「天地開創，人神慶仰，宜存問遠方，宣廣慈澤」。

translations.literal: 」The matters submitted number eleven in all. First, he held that 「Heaven and earth newly opened, men and spirits rejoice and look up; one should send inquiries to distant regions and spread broad merciful grace.」
translations.idiomatic: 」The memorial sets forth eleven points in all. First: 「Heaven and earth are newly opened; men and spirits rejoice and look up—send inquiries to distant regions and spread broad merciful grace.」

sentences.zh: 其二，以爲「京師浩大，遠近所歸，宜遣醫藥，問其疾苦。

translations.literal: Second, he held that 「The capital is vast; near and far turn to it—one should dispatch physicians and medicines and ask after their suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Second: 「The capital is vast, and near and far turn to it—dispatch physicians and medicines and ask after their suffering.

sentences.zh: 年九十以上及六疾不能自存者，隨宜量賜」。

translations.literal: Those ninety years of age and above, and those with the six afflictions who cannot support themselves, should receive gifts measured as fit.」
translations.idiomatic: Those ninety and above, and those with the six afflictions who cannot support themselves, should receive gifts as circumstances require.」

sentences.zh: 其三，以爲「宋氏赦令，蒙原者寡。

translations.literal: Third, he held that 「Song's amnesty edicts—few received pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Third: 「Under the Song, amnesty edicts brought pardon to few.

sentences.zh: 愚謂今下赦書，宜令事實相副」。

translations.literal: This fool holds that the amnesty now issued should make deed and word match.」
translations.idiomatic: This fool holds that the amnesty now issued should match deed to word.」

sentences.zh: 其四，以爲「匈奴未滅，劉昶猶存，秋風揚塵，容能送死。

translations.literal: Fourth, he held that 「The Xiongnu are not yet destroyed; Liu Chang still lives; autumn wind raises dust—they may yet see their end.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth: 「The Xiongnu are not yet destroyed; Liu Chang still lives; when autumn wind raises dust, they may yet fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 境上諸城，宜應嚴備，特簡雄略，以待事機，資實所須，皆宜豫辦」。

translations.literal: The frontier towns should answer with strict preparation; specially choose men of bold strategy to await the moment; all supplies needed should be prepared beforehand.」
translations.idiomatic: Frontier towns should stand in strict readiness; choose men of bold strategy to await the moment; every supply needed should be prepared in advance.」

sentences.zh: 其五，以爲「宜除宋氏大明泰始以來諸苛政細制，以崇簡易」。

translations.literal: Fifth, he held that 「One should remove the harsh policies and minute regulations since Song's Daming and Taishi reigns, to exalt simplicity and ease.」
translations.idiomatic: Fifth: 「Remove the harsh policies and minute regulations since Song's Daming and Taishi reigns, and exalt simplicity and ease.」

sentences.zh: 其六，以爲「凡諸土木之費，且可權停」。

translations.literal: Sixth, he held that 「All expenses for earthworks and timber may for now be suspended by authority.」
translations.idiomatic: Sixth: 「All expenses for earthworks and timber may for now be suspended.」

sentences.zh: 其七，以爲「帝子王姬，宜崇儉約」。

translations.literal: Seventh, he held that 「Imperial sons and royal daughters should be exalted in thrift and restraint.」
translations.idiomatic: Seventh: 「Imperial sons and royal daughters should be held to thrift and restraint.」

sentences.zh: 其八，以爲「宜詔百官及府州郡縣，各貢讜言，以弘唐虞之美」。

translations.literal: Eighth, he held that 「One should decree to the hundred officials and to prefectures, provinces, and counties that each present forthright counsel, to enlarge the beauty of Yao and Shun.」
translations.idiomatic: Eighth: 「Decree to the hundred officials and to prefectures, provinces, and counties that each present forthright counsel, to enlarge the beauty of Yao and Shun.」

sentences.zh: 其九，以爲「忠貞孝悌，宜擢以殊階，清儉苦節，應授以民政」。

translations.literal: Ninth, he held that 「Loyalty, integrity, filial piety, and brotherhood should be raised to special rank; purity, thrift, and bitter integrity should receive civil administration.」
translations.idiomatic: Ninth: 「Loyalty, integrity, filial piety, and brotherhood should be raised to special rank; purity, thrift, and bitter integrity should receive charge of civil affairs.」

sentences.zh: 其十，以爲「革命惟始，天地大慶，宜時擇才辨，北使匈奴」。

translations.literal: Tenth, he held that 「The revolution has only begun; Heaven and earth hold a great rejoicing—at this time choose men of talent and discernment to go north as envoys to the Xiongnu.」
translations.idiomatic: Tenth: 「The revolution has only begun; Heaven and earth hold a great rejoicing—at this time choose men of talent and discernment to go north as envoys to the Xiongnu.」

sentences.zh: 其十一，以爲「交州險敻，要荒之表，宋末政苛，遂至怨叛。

translations.literal: Eleventh, he held that 「Jiaozhou is perilous and remote, on the outer edge of the wild borderlands; late Song government was harsh, and so resentment rose to rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh: 「Jiaozhou is perilous and remote, on the outer edge of the wild borderlands; late Song government was harsh, and resentment rose to rebellion.

sentences.zh: 今大化創始，宜懷以恩德，未應遠勞將士，搖動邊氓。

translations.literal: Now the great transformation has only begun—one should embrace them with grace and virtue; one should not yet trouble soldiers from afar and shake the frontier folk.
translations.idiomatic: Now the great transformation has only begun—embrace them with grace and virtue; do not yet trouble soldiers from afar and shake the frontier people.

sentences.zh: 且彼土所出，唯有珠寶，實非聖朝所須之急。

translations.literal: Moreover, what that land produces is only pearls and gems—truly not what the sage court urgently needs.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what that land yields is only pearls and gems—not what the sage court urgently needs.

sentences.zh: 討伐之事，謂宜且停」。

translations.literal: The matter of punitive expedition—I hold it should for now be stopped.」
translations.idiomatic: The punitive expedition—I hold it should for now be stopped.」

sentences.zh: 又撰《賢聖雜語》奏之，託以諷諫。

translations.literal: He also compiled Miscellaneous Sayings of Worthies and Sages and submitted it, using it to convey remonstrance by indirection.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled Miscellaneous Sayings of Worthies and Sages and submitted it, using it to remonstrate by indirection.

sentences.zh: 上答曰：「省所獻雜語，竝列聖之明規，衆智之深軌。

translations.literal: The emperor replied: 「I have reviewed the miscellaneous sayings you submitted—they all array the bright norms of the sages and the deep tracks of the many wise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: 「I have reviewed the miscellaneous sayings you submitted—they array the bright norms of the sages and the deep tracks of the many wise.

sentences.zh: 卿能憲章先範，纂鏤情識，忠款旣昭，淵誠肅著，當以周旋，無忘聽覽也。

translations.literal: You can take the former models as law, carve and inlay feeling and knowledge; loyal sincerity is already bright, profound sincerity solemnly shown—you shall have my constant regard, and I shall not forget to hear and read.」
translations.idiomatic: You can take the former models as law and carve your feeling into knowledge; loyal sincerity is already bright, profound sincerity solemnly shown—you shall have my constant regard, and I shall not forget to hear and read.」

sentences.zh: 」又諫起宣陽門；

translations.literal: 」He also remonstrated against building the Xuanyang Gate;
translations.idiomatic: 」He also remonstrated against building the Xuanyang Gate;

sentences.zh: 表陳宜明守宰賞罰；

translations.literal: in a memorial he stated that rewards and punishments for prefects and magistrates should be made clear;
translations.idiomatic: in a memorial he stated that rewards and punishments for prefects and magistrates should be made clear;

sentences.zh: 立學校，制齊禮；

translations.literal: schools should be established and Qi rites regulated;
translations.idiomatic: schools should be established and Qi rites regulated;

sentences.zh: 廣開賔館，以接荒民。

translations.literal: guest houses should be broadly opened to receive the folk of the wild borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: guest houses should be broadly opened to receive the folk of the wild borderlands.

sentences.zh: 上又答曰：「具卿忠讜之懷。

translations.literal: The emperor again replied: 「I have taken in full your loyal, forthright heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again replied: 「I have taken in full your loyal, forthright heart.

sentences.zh: 夫賞罰以懲守宰，飾館以待遐荒。

translations.literal: Rewards and punishments to chasten prefects and magistrates, ornamented lodges to await the distant wilds—
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments to chasten prefects and magistrates, ornamented lodges to await the distant wilds—

sentences.zh: 皆古之善政，吾所宜勉。

translations.literal: all are good government of antiquity; they are what I should strive for.
translations.idiomatic: all are good government of antiquity; they are what I should strive for.

sentences.zh: 更撰新禮，或非易制。

translations.literal: To draft new rites anew may not be easy to accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: To draft new rites anew may not be easy to accomplish.

sentences.zh: 國學之美，已敕公卿。

translations.literal: The beauty of the state academy—I have already charged the excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: The beauty of the state academy—I have already charged the excellencies.

sentences.zh: 宣陽門今敕停。

translations.literal: The Xuanyang Gate—I now decree it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanyang Gate—I now decree it stopped.

sentences.zh: 寡德多闕，思復有聞。」

translations.literal: My few virtues have many lacks; I wish again to hear.」
translations.idiomatic: My few virtues have many lacks; I wish again to hear.」

sentences.zh: 善明身長七尺九寸，質素不好聲色，所居茅齋斧木而已，牀榻机案，不加刬削。

translations.literal: Shanming was seven feet nine inches tall, plain by nature and not fond of sound or color; where he lived was only a thatched hut with axe-hewn timber; bed, couch, table, and desk received no planing.
translations.idiomatic: Shanming stood seven feet nine inches, plain by nature and no lover of sound or color; he lived in a thatched hut with axe-hewn timber alone; bed, couch, table, and desk went unplaned.

sentences.zh: 少與崔祖思友善，祖思出爲青、冀二州，善明遺書曰：「昔時之遊，于今邈矣。

translations.literal: In youth he was friendly with Cui Zusi; when Zusi went out as inspector of Qing and Ji, Shanming sent him a letter saying: 「The wanderings of old are far away now.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was friendly with Cui Zusi; when Zusi went out as inspector of Qing and Ji, Shanming sent him a letter saying, 「The wanderings of old are far away now.

sentences.zh: 或攜手春林，或負杖秋澗，逐清風於林杪，追素月於園垂，如何故人，徂落殆盡。

translations.literal: Sometimes we walked hand in hand in spring woods, sometimes leaned on staves in autumn streams; we chased the clear wind at the treetops and pursued the plain moon at the garden eaves—how is it that old friends have mostly gone to their fall?
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes we walked hand in hand in spring woods, sometimes leaned on staves in autumn streams; we chased the clear wind at the treetops and the plain moon along the garden eaves—how is it that old friends have mostly gone to their fall?

sentences.zh: 足下方擁旄北服，吾剖竹南甸，相去千里，閒以江山，人生如寄，來會何時。

translations.literal: You now hold the staff in the northern realm; I govern by split bamboo in the southern district; a thousand li apart, with rivers and mountains between—life is lodging; when shall we meet again?
translations.idiomatic: You now hold the banner in the northern realm; I govern the southern district by split bamboo; a thousand li apart, rivers and mountains between—life is lodging; when shall we meet again?

sentences.zh: 嘗覽書史，數千年來，略在眼中矣。

translations.literal: I have browsed books and histories; several thousand years lie, in brief, before my eyes.
translations.idiomatic: I have browsed books and histories; several thousand years lie, in brief, before my eyes.

sentences.zh: 歷代參差，萬理同異。

translations.literal: Dynasties differ in their rise and fall; the ten thousand principles share sameness and difference.
translations.idiomatic: Dynasties differ in their rise and fall; the ten thousand principles share sameness and difference.

sentences.zh: 夫龍虎風雲之契，亂極必夷之幾，古今豈殊，此實一揆。

translations.literal: The bond of dragon and tiger, wind and cloud; the moment when chaos reaches its limit and must turn to peace—past and present, how could they differ? In truth it is one measure.
translations.idiomatic: The bond of dragon and tiger, wind and cloud; the moment when chaos reaches its limit and must turn to peace—past and present, how could they differ? In truth it is one measure.

sentences.zh: 日者沈攸之擁長蛇於外，粲、秉復爲異識所推；

translations.literal: Recently Shen Youzhi coiled his long serpent without; Can and Bing were again pushed by rival factions;
translations.idiomatic: Only lately Shen Youzhi had coiled his armies beyond the walls, while Yuan Can and Liu Bing were again hoisted up by rival factions;
