sentences.zh: 唯有京鎮，創爲聖基。

translations.literal: only the capital commandery laid the sacred foundation.
translations.idiomatic: only the capital region held firm as the throne's foundation.

sentences.zh: 遂乃擢吾爲首佐，授吾以大郡，付吾關中，委吾留任。

translations.literal: Then they raised me as chief aide, gave me a great commandery, entrusted me with the central marches, and left me in post.
translations.idiomatic: Then they lifted me to chief counselor, granted a great commandery, placed the heartland marches in my hands, and kept me at my post.

sentences.zh: 旣不辦有抽劔兩城之用，橫槊搴旗之能，徒以挈瓶小智，名參佐命，常恐朝露一下，深恩不酬。

translations.literal: Having neither skill to draw the sword and recover two cities nor talent to pole a spear and seize banners, I had only the petty wit of one who carries the water jar—yet my name stood among the founders' aides; I always feared that at one fall of morning dew I could not repay deep grace.
translations.idiomatic: I could neither storm two cities at a stroke nor wrest banners with a levelled spear—only bottle-carrier cleverness, yet my name was counted among the founders' counselors. I lived in dread that dawn dew might fall once and leave their grace unpaid.

sentences.zh: 憂深責重，轉不可據，還視生世，倍無次緒。

translations.literal: Worry deep and burden heavy, I turned all the more unsteady; looking back on life, I was twice without order.
translations.idiomatic: Burden and worry grew until I could scarcely stand; looking back on my days, I found them twice as tangled.

sentences.zh: 藿羹布被，猶篤鄙好，惡色憎聲，暮齡尤甚。

translations.literal: Chenopodium broth and cloth quilts—I still clung to vulgar tastes; ugly colors and hateful sounds I hated all the more in late age.
translations.idiomatic: I still clung to coarse broth and plain quilts, still shunned gaud and clamor—and in old age the distaste only sharpened.

sentences.zh: 出蕃不與台輔別，入國不與公卿遊，孤立天地之閒，無猜無託，唯知奉主以忠，事親以孝，臨民以潔，居家以儉。

translations.literal: Going out to the frontier I did not take leave of the chief ministers; entering court I did not consort with the grandees—alone between heaven and earth, without suspicion and without patron, knowing only to serve the lord with loyalty, parents with filial piety, the people with clean rule, and the household with thrift.
translations.idiomatic: When I left for the frontier I did not bid the chief ministers farewell; when I entered court I did not keep company with the grandees—alone between heaven and earth, without ally or patron, serving my lord in loyalty, my kin in filial piety, the people in clean government, and my home in thrift.

sentences.zh: 足下今鳴笳舊郷，衣繡故國，宋季荼毒之悲已蒙蘇泰，河朔倒懸之苦方須救鬬。

translations.literal: You now sound the pipes in your old home and wear brocade in your native state; Song's bitter suffering has met Su Qin's revival, while the north of the river still hangs inverted and awaits rescue in battle.
translations.idiomatic: You now sound the pipes in your old country and wear brocade in your native land: Song's poisoned grief has tasted Su Qin's healing, yet the north of the Yellow River still hangs upside down and cries out for deliverance in arms.

sentences.zh: 遣遊辯之士，爲郷導之使，輕裝啓行，經營舊壤，令泗上歸業，稷下還風，君欲誰讓邪？

translations.literal: Send eloquent envoys as guides for the homeland; set out in light gear and reclaim the old soil—let the Si basin return to its livelihood and Jixia recover its wind. To whom would you yield the merit?
translations.idiomatic: Send eloquent men as homeland guides; march light and work the old ground again—let the Si country take up its trades and Jixia breathe its old spirit. Whom would you leave the credit to?

sentences.zh: 聊送諸心，敬申貧贈。」

translations.literal: Here I offer my whole heart; respectfully I present this poor gift.」
translations.idiomatic: Here I send you my whole heart; respectfully I offer this humble parting gift.」

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: He died at forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 遺命薄殯。

translations.literal: His testament ordered a spare burial.
translations.idiomatic: By his own order he was buried plainly.

sentences.zh: 贈錢三萬，布五十匹。

translations.literal: Thirty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth were granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted thirty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「善明忠誠夙亮，幹力兼宣，豫經夷嶮，勤績昭著。

translations.literal: Another edict said: 「Shanming's loyalty was bright from the first, his energy and strength alike proclaimed; he passed through perilous straits and his diligent merit shone clear.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict read: 「Shanming's loyalty shone early, his force and counsel alike outstanding; he bore the bitter passes and his service stood clear.

sentences.zh: 不幸殞喪，痛悼于懷。

translations.literal: Untimely he fell and died; grief lodges in Our breast.
translations.idiomatic: He has fallen untimely, and grief lodges in Our heart.

sentences.zh: 贈左將軍、豫州刺史，諡烈伯。

translations.literal: We posthumously grant Left General and Inspector of Yuzhou, with the posthumous title Baron of Lie.」
translations.idiomatic: We posthumously appoint him Left General and Inspector of Yuzhou, with the posthumous title Baron of Lie.」

sentences.zh: 」子滌嗣。

translations.literal: His son Di inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Di succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 善明家無遺儲，唯有書八千卷。

translations.literal: Shanming's house had no stored wealth—only eight thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: Shanming left no stored wealth in his house—only eight thousand scrolls of books.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞其清貧，賜滌家葛塘屯穀五百斛。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor heard of his clean poverty, he granted Di's household five hundred hu of grain from the Getang estate.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of his stark poverty, the Grand Ancestor granted Di's household five hundred hu of grain from the Getang estate.

sentences.zh: 善明從弟僧副，官至前將軍，封豐陽男，三百戶。

translations.literal: Shanming's cousin Sengfu reached the post of front general and was enfeoffed as Baron of Fengyang with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Shanming's cousin Sengfu rose to front general and was enfeoffed as Baron of Fengyang with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: ，爲巴西梓潼二郡太守，卒。

translations.literal: He served as administrator of the two commanderies Brazil and Zitong and died.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Brazil and Zitong and died in office.

sentences.zh: 蘇侃

translations.literal: Su Kan
translations.idiomatic: Su Kan

sentences.zh: 蘇侃字休烈，武邑人也。

translations.literal: Su Kan, styled Xiulie, was a man of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Su Kan, styled Xiulie, came from Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 祖護，本郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hu was administrator of the native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hu was administrator of the home commandery.

sentences.zh: 父端，州治中。

translations.literal: His father Duan was provincial clerical director.
translations.idiomatic: His father Duan was provincial clerical director.

sentences.zh: 侃涉獵書傳，出身正員將軍，補長城令。

translations.literal: Kan ranged through the classics and histories, entered service as a regular general, and was appointed magistrate of Changcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kan ranged through the classics and histories, entered service as a regular general, and was posted as magistrate of Changcheng.

sentences.zh: 薛安都反，引侃爲其府參軍，使掌書記。

translations.literal: When Xue Andu rebelled, he recruited Kan as staff aide and had him keep the records.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Andu rebelled, he took Kan onto his staff as aide and set him to keep the records.

sentences.zh: 安都降虜，侃自拔南歸。

translations.literal: When Andu surrendered to the northerners, Kan broke free and fled south alone.
translations.idiomatic: When Andu went over to the northerners, Kan cut himself loose and fled south alone.

sentences.zh: 除積射將軍。

translations.literal: He was made general of scattered shooters.
translations.idiomatic: He was named general of scattered shooters.

sentences.zh: 遇太祖在淮上，便自委結。

translations.literal: He met the Grand Ancestor on the Huai and at once pledged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He met the Grand Ancestor on the Huai and at once pledged his service.

sentences.zh: 上鎮淮陰，以侃詳密，取爲冠軍錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When the Lord garrisoned Huaiyin, he took Kan for his meticulous care and made him registrar on the champion's staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lord held Huaiyin, he valued Kan's thoroughness and made him registrar on the champion's staff.

sentences.zh: 是時張永、沈攸之敗後，新失淮北，始遣上北戍，不滿千人，每歲秋冬閒，邊淮騷動，恒恐虜至。

translations.literal: At that time, after Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi had been defeated and the north of the Huai was newly lost, the Lord was first sent to guard the northern line with fewer than a thousand men; each year between autumn and winter the frontier along the Huai stirred, and he constantly feared the northerners would come.
translations.idiomatic: This was just after Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi were broken and Huaibei was lost; the Lord was first sent to hold the northern line with fewer than a thousand men. Every year between autumn and winter the Huai frontier flared, and he lived in dread of a northern strike.

sentences.zh: 上廣遣偵候，安集荒餘，又營繕城府。

translations.literal: The Lord widely sent scouts, pacified the scattered survivors, and also repaired walls and ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord sent scouts far abroad, gathered in the scattered survivors, and rebuilt walls and ramparts.

sentences.zh: 上在兵中久，見疑於時，乃作《塞客吟》以喻志曰：「寶緯紊宗，神經越序。

translations.literal: The Lord had long been in the army and was viewed with suspicion by the age; he then composed the 「Ballad of the Frontier Guest」 to declare his intent, saying: 「The royal cords tangle the lineage; spirit lines cross their proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Long in the field, the Lord was eyed with suspicion; he wrote the 「Ballad of the Frontier Guest」 to lay bare his heart, saying: 「The throne's cords knot the royal line; heaven's channels run out of their proper course.

sentences.zh: 德晦河、晉，力宣江、楚。

translations.literal: Virtue lies hidden in the Yellow and Jin lands; force is proclaimed on the Yangtze and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue dims along the Yellow and Jin; power speaks on the Yangtze and Chu.

sentences.zh: 雲雷兆壯，天山繇武。

translations.literal: Clouds and thunder augur vigor; Heaven Mountain summons arms.
translations.idiomatic: Clouds and thunder betoken might; Heaven Mountain calls forth war.

sentences.zh: 直髮指秦關，凝精越漢渚。

translations.literal: With hair unbound I point at the Qin passes; with spirit gathered I cross the Han ford.
translations.idiomatic: Bareheaded I aim at the Qin passes; with gathered will I ford the Han streams.

sentences.zh: 秋風起，塞草衰，鵰鴻思，邊馬悲。

translations.literal: The autumn wind rises; frontier grass withers; the hawk and wild goose yearn; border horses grieve.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn wind rises; frontier grass fades; hawk and wild goose ache with longing; border horses grieve.

sentences.zh: 平原千里顧，但見轉蓬飛。

translations.literal: Gazing over a thousand li of plain, one sees only tumbleweed flying.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand li of plain, only tumbleweed flies in the eye.

sentences.zh: 星嚴海淨，月澈河明。

translations.literal: Stars stand stern; the sea is clear; the moon is limpid; the river bright.
translations.idiomatic: Stars stand sharp; the sea lies clear; the moon runs bright; the river shines.

sentences.zh: 清輝映幕，素液凝庭。

translations.literal: Clear radiance shines on the tent curtain; pure dew congeals in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Clear light washes the tent flap; white dew gathers in the court.

sentences.zh: 金笳夜厲，羽轊晨征。

translations.literal: Golden reed-pipes cry sharp at night; feathered oars set out at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Golden pipes wail through the night; feathered oars march at dawn.

sentences.zh: 斡晴潭而悵泗，枻松洲而悼情。

translations.literal: Mooring on the clear pool, I grieve for the Si; rowing the pine islet, I mourn in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: I moor on the bright pool and ache for the Si; I ply the pine islet and mourn in my breast.

sentences.zh: 蘭涵風而瀉豔，菊籠泉而散英。

translations.literal: Orchids hold the wind and pour out splendor; chrysanthemums cage the spring and scatter their blooms.
translations.idiomatic: Orchids drink the wind and spill their color; chrysanthemums cup the spring and scatter fragrance.

sentences.zh: 曲繞首燕之歎，吹軫絕越之聲。

translations.literal: A tune winds through the lament of Shouyan; the flute sounds the music of vanished Yue.
translations.idiomatic: The tune circles Shouyan's sigh; the flute plays the lost music of Yue.

sentences.zh: 欷園琴之孤弄，想庭藿之餘馨。

translations.literal: I sigh at the garden zither's lonely playing; I recall the courtyard bean's lingering scent.
translations.idiomatic: I sigh at the garden zither's solitary song; I think of the courtyard bean's last sweetness.

sentences.zh: 青關望斷，白日西斜。

translations.literal: The green pass sight is cut off; the white sun slopes west.
translations.idiomatic: The green pass fades from view; the white sun leans west.

sentences.zh: 恬源靚霧，壟首暉霞。

translations.literal: The peaceful spring is fair in mist; the mound's brow glows with rose clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Still springs gleam through mist; the tomb ridge wears dawn's rose light.

sentences.zh: 戒旋鷁，躍還波，情綿綿而方遠，思裊裊而遂多。

translations.literal: Wary, the osprey wheels back; leaping, it returns on the waves; feeling stretches far and farther; thought threads on and grows.
translations.idiomatic: Wary, the fishhawk wheels home; it leaps back across the waves; longing trails farther still; memory winds on and on.

sentences.zh: 粵擊秦中之筑，因爲塞上之歌。

translations.literal: Hence I strike the Qin-land zhu; thus I make this song of the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: So I strike the Qin-country zhu drum and shape this ballad of the frontier pass.

sentences.zh: 歌曰：朝發兮江泉，日夕兮陵山。

translations.literal: The song says: Setting out at dawn from the river springs, by sunset reaching the ridge mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The song runs: At dawn we leave the river springs; by sunset we stand on the ridge mountains.

sentences.zh: 驚飆兮瀄汨，淮流兮潺湲。

translations.literal: Startled gale, rushing and swirling; Huai currents murmur and ripple.
translations.idiomatic: A startled gale rushes and swirls; the Huai murmurs on in rippling flood.

sentences.zh: 胡埃兮雲聚，楚旆兮星懸。

translations.literal: Barbarian dust like gathered clouds; Chu banners hang like stars.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian dust gathers like clouds; Chu banners hang like stars in the sky.

sentences.zh: 愁墉兮思宇，惻愴兮何言。

translations.literal: Grief for the ramparts, longing for the hall; anguish—what words can tell it?
translations.idiomatic: Grief for the ramparts, longing for the hall—anguish beyond any words.

sentences.zh: 定寰中之逸鑒，審雕陵之迷泉。

translations.literal: He fixed the transcendent mirror within the realm and examined the bewildering spring at Diaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He set the far-seeing mirror within the realm and weighed the hidden spring at Diaoling.

sentences.zh: 悟樊籠之或累，悵遐心以栖玄。

translations.literal: Awakening that the barred cage may burden one, he let his distant heart rest in mystery.
translations.idiomatic: He saw how the barred cage can burden a man, and gave his far-ranging heart to rest in mystery.

sentences.zh: 」侃達上此旨，更自勤勵。

translations.literal: 」Kan offered this intent to the Sovereign and redoubled his own diligence.
translations.idiomatic: 」Kan laid this meaning before the throne and drove himself harder still.

sentences.zh: 委以府事，深見知待。

translations.literal: He was entrusted with bureau affairs and deeply trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau affairs were placed in his hands, and he was warmly trusted.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，巴西人李承明作亂，太祖議遣侃銜使慰勞，還除羽林監，加建武將軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanhui, Li Chengming of Brazil rose in rebellion; the Grand Ancestor considered sending Kan as credentialed envoy to comfort and reassure the troops. On his return he was made director of the feathered forest guard and further named General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Yuanhui, Li Chengming of Brazil rebelled; the Grand Ancestor meant to send Kan with credentials to comfort the armies. When he came back he was named director of the feathered forest guard and raised to General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 桂陽之難，上復以侃爲平南錄事，領軍主，從頓新亭，使分金銀賦賜諸將。

translations.literal: In the Guiyang crisis the Sovereign again made Kan recorder on the southern pacification staff, with command of a military division; he followed the court to camp at Xinting and was ordered to divide gold and silver for gifts and grants to the generals.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guiyang trouble the Sovereign again set Kan as recorder on the southern pacification staff, leading a command; he followed the court to Xinting and was told to parcel out gold and silver as gifts for the generals.

sentences.zh: 事寧，除步兵校尉，出爲綏虜將軍、山陽太守，清脩有治理，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was made commandant of foot soldiers, then sent out as General Who Comforts Captives and administrator of Shanyang; pure in conduct and skilled in rule, the people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: After peace returned he became commandant of foot soldiers, then went out as General Who Comforts Captives and administrator of Shanyang—clean in his ways, firm in governance, and beloved by the people.

sentences.zh: 進號龍驤將軍，除前軍將軍。

translations.literal: His title advanced to General Who Dragon-Prances, and he was made vanguard general.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to General Who Dragon-Prances and named vanguard general.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，除侃游擊將軍，遷太祖驃騎諮議，領錄事，除黃門郎，復爲太祖太尉諮議。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair broke out, Kan was made mobile-strike general, moved to consultative officer of the Grand Ancestor's Rapid Cavalry, with charge of recorder duties, made gentleman of the yellow gate, and again consultative officer to the Grand Ancestor as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rose, Kan was named mobile-strike general, then consultative officer on the Grand Ancestor's Rapid Cavalry staff, keeping recorder duties; he became gentleman of the yellow gate and again consultative officer to the Grand Ancestor as grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 侃事上旣久，備悉起居，乃與丘巨源撰《蕭太尉記》，載上征伐之功。

translations.literal: Kan had long served the Sovereign and knew the daily round in full; he and Qiu Juyuan compiled Records of Grand Marshal Xiao, setting down the Sovereign's campaigns and achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Kan had served the throne for years and knew its daily round by heart; with Qiu Juyuan he compiled Records of Grand Marshal Xiao, recording the Sovereign's wars and merit.

sentences.zh: 以功封新建縣侯，五百戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as marquis of Xinjian county, five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed as marquis of Xinjian, five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 齊臺建，爲黃門郎，領射聲校尉，任以心膂。

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was established he was gentleman of the yellow gate and commandant of the sound-shooters, trusted as a man of the inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regime was set up he was gentleman of the yellow gate and commandant of the sound-shooters, counted among the Sovereign's closest men.

sentences.zh: 上卽位，侃撰聖皇瑞命記一卷奏之。

translations.literal: When the Sovereign took the throne, Kan composed and presented one scroll of Records of the Sage Emperor's Auspicious Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: At the Sovereign's accession Kan wrote and presented one scroll of Records of the Sage Emperor's Auspicious Mandate.

sentences.zh: ，卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: , he died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, at fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 上惜之甚至，追贈輔國將軍、梁南秦二州刺史，諡質侯。

translations.literal: The Sovereign grieved for him deeply, posthumously enfeoffed him as general who supports the state and inspector of Liang and southern Qin, and gave the posthumous title Marquis Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The throne mourned him deeply, raised him posthumously to general who supports the state and inspector of Liang and southern Qin, and gave him the posthumous title Marquis Zhi.

sentences.zh: 弟烈，字休文，初爲東莞令，張永鎮軍中兵，累至山陽太守，寧朔將軍，游擊將軍。

translations.literal: His younger brother Lie, styled Xiuwen, was at first magistrate of Dongguan, then a soldier of Zhang Yong's garrison headquarters, rising in stages to administrator of Shanyang, General Who Pacifies the North, and mobile-strike general.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Lie, styled Xiuwen, began as magistrate of Dongguan, then served in Zhang Yong's garrison staff, rising step by step to administrator of Shanyang, General Who Pacifies the North, and mobile-strike general.

sentences.zh: 袁粲起事，太祖先遣烈助防城，仍隨諸將平石頭，封吉陽縣男。

translations.literal: When Yuan Can rose, the Grand Ancestor first sent Lie to help defend the city, then had him follow the generals in pacifying Shitou; he was enfeoffed as baron of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Can rebelled, the Grand Ancestor first sent Lie to aid in the city's defense, then had him follow the generals in taking Shitou; he was enfeoffed as baron of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 建元中，爲假節、督巴州軍事、巴州刺史、巴東太守，寧朔將軍如故。

translations.literal: In the Jianyuan era he held acting credentials, oversaw Ba province military affairs, was inspector of Ba and administrator of Badong, his rank as General Who Pacifies the North unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianyuan he bore acting credentials, oversaw Ba province's armies, and held inspector of Ba with the post of administrator of Badong, still General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 永明中，至平西司馬、陳留太守，卒官。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era he reached the post of marshal of the west-pacifying army and administrator of Chenliu, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming he rose to marshal of the west-pacifying army and administrator of Chenliu, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 垣榮祖

translations.literal: Yuan Rongzu
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Rongzu

sentences.zh: 垣榮祖字華先，下邳人，五兵尚書崇祖從父兄也。

translations.literal: Yuan Rongzu, styled Huaxian, was a native of Xiapi; he was the elder cousin on his father's side of Yuan Chongzu, minister of the five armaments.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Rongzu, styled Huaxian, came from Xiapi—the elder cousin of Yuan Chongzu, minister of the five armaments.

sentences.zh: 父諒之，宋北中郎府參軍。

translations.literal: His father Liangzhi had been a staff officer in the Song northern center army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liangzhi had served as a staff officer in the Song northern center army headquarters.

sentences.zh: 榮祖少學騎馬及射，或謂之曰：「武事可畏，何不學書。

translations.literal: As a youth Rongzu studied horsemanship and archery; someone said to him: 「Martial affairs are perilous—why not study books instead?
translations.idiomatic: In youth Rongzu trained in riding and archery; someone told him: 「War is a fearsome trade—why not take up books instead?

sentences.zh: 」榮祖曰：「昔曹操、曹丕上馬橫槊，下馬談論，此於天下可不負飲食矣。

translations.literal: 」Rongzu said: 「Of old Cao Cao and Cao Pi mounted with spear across the saddle and dismounted to hold discourse—by that alone a man need not fail the world's bread.
translations.idiomatic: 」Rongzu said: 「Cao Cao and Cao Pi rode with spear laid across the saddle and dismounted to talk policy—that alone was enough to earn their bread under heaven.

sentences.zh: 君輩無自全之伎，何異犬羊乎！」

translations.literal: You gentlemen have no art by which to save yourselves—how are you not like dogs and sheep?」
translations.idiomatic: You have no skill to keep yourselves alive—what are you but dogs and sheep?」

sentences.zh: 宋孝建中，州辟主簿，爲後軍參軍。

translations.literal: In the Xiaojian era of Emperor Xiao of Song the province recruited him as chief clerk, and he became a rear-army staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiao's Xiaojian reign the province took him as chief clerk, then made him a rear-army staff officer.

sentences.zh: 伯父豫州刺史護之子襲祖爲淮陽太守，宋孝武以事徙之嶺南，護之不食而死。

translations.literal: His uncle's son Xizu, son of the inspector of Yu Hu, was administrator of Huaiyang; Emperor Xiaowu of Song, on account of the affair, banished him to the far south, and Hu starved himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Xizu, son of Inspector of Yu Hu, held Huaiyang as administrator; Emperor Xiaowu, over the matter, exiled him to the far south, and Hu refused food until he died.

sentences.zh: 帝疾篤，又遣使殺襲祖，襲祖臨死，與榮祖書曰：「弟常勸我危行言遜，今果敗矣。」

translations.literal: When the emperor lay gravely ill he again sent an envoy to kill Xizu; facing death, Xizu wrote to Rongzu: 「You always urged me to walk on the edge yet speak with restraint—now the ruin has come, as you said.」
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor lay dying he sent again to kill Xizu; at the end Xizu wrote Rongzu: 「You always told me to court danger yet speak softly—now it has failed, just as you warned.」

sentences.zh: 明帝初卽位，四方反，除榮祖冗從僕射，遣還徐州說刺史薛安都曰：「天之所廢，誰能興之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign, with rebellion on every side, Rongzu was made supernumerary attendant master of ceremonies and sent back to Xu to persuade Inspector Xue Andu, saying: 「What heaven casts down, who can raise up again?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming first took the throne and the realm rose on every side, Rongzu was named supernumerary attendant master of ceremonies and sent back to Xu to speak with Inspector Xue Andu: 「What heaven has cast aside—who can set it upright again?

sentences.zh: 使君今不同八百諸侯，如民所見，非計中也。

translations.literal: My lord, if you do not now stand with the eight hundred lords of old, as the people see it, that is no sound plan.」
translations.idiomatic: My lord, if you will not now join the eight hundred lords of old, the people will read it as folly.」

sentences.zh: 」安都曰：「天命有在，今京都無百里地，莫論攻圍取勝，自可拍手笑殺。

translations.literal: Andu said: 「Heaven's mandate has its holder; today the capital has not a hundred li of ground—never mind siege and victory, one may simply clap one's hands and laugh them to death.
translations.idiomatic: Andu said: 「The mandate has its man; the capital today holds less than a hundred li—never mind storming walls or winning battles, one need only clap hands and laugh them dead.

sentences.zh: 且我不欲負孝武。

translations.literal: Besides, I do not wish to betray Emperor Xiaowu.」
translations.idiomatic: And I will not betray Emperor Xiaowu.」

sentences.zh: 」榮祖曰：「孝武之行，足致餘殃。

translations.literal: Rongzu said: 「Emperor Xiaowu's conduct was enough to bring lingering ruin.」
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu said: 「Emperor Xiaowu's ways were ruin enough to outlast his reign.」

sentences.zh: 今雖天下雷同，正是速死，無能爲也。

translations.literal: 「Though all under heaven now echo the same cry, that is only a swift road to death—nothing can be done.」
translations.idiomatic: 「Though the realm shouts as one today, that is only the quick road to death—no one can prevail.」

sentences.zh: 」安都曰：「不知諸人云何，我不畏此。

translations.literal: Andu said: 「I do not know how the others stand; I do not fear that.」
translations.idiomatic: Andu said: 「I cannot tell what the rest intend—I do not fear them.」

sentences.zh: 大蹄馬在近，急便作計。

translations.literal: The great-hoof horses are near—decide at once.」
translations.idiomatic: The steppe horses are close—act now.」

sentences.zh: 」榮祖被拘不得還，因收集部曲，爲安都將領。

translations.literal: Rongzu was detained and could not return; he therefore gathered his followers and became a commander under Andu.
translations.idiomatic: Held fast and unable to go south again, Rongzu rallied his household troops and served Andu as a commander.

sentences.zh: 假署冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He received an acting appointment as champion general.
translations.idiomatic: He was given acting rank as champion general.

sentences.zh: 安都引虜入彭城，榮祖攜家屬南奔朐山，虜遣騎追之不及。

translations.literal: When Andu brought the barbarians into Pengcheng, Rongzu fled south with his household to Qushan; the barbarians sent horsemen in pursuit but could not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: When Andu led the northerners into Pengcheng, Rongzu took his family south to Qushan; pursuit riders could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 榮祖懼得罪，乃逃遁淮上。

translations.literal: Fearing punishment, he then fled along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing court punishment, he hid along the Huai.

sentences.zh: 太祖在淮陰，榮祖歸附，上保持之。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor was at Huaiyin; Rongzu came over to him, and the Sovereign sheltered him.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor was at Huaiyin; Rongzu submitted, and the Sovereign kept him close.

sentences.zh: 及明帝崩，太祖書送榮祖詣僕射褚淵，除寧朔將軍、東海太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, the Grand Ancestor sent Rongzu by letter to Vicegerent Chu Yuan and had him made General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Ming's death the Grand Ancestor sent Rongzu to Vicegerent Chu Yuan with a letter of introduction and had him named General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 淵謂之曰：「蕭公稱卿幹略，故以此郡相處。」

translations.literal: Chu said to him: 「Lord Xiao praised your capacity and plan—hence this commandery was given you.」
translations.idiomatic: Chu told him: 「Lord Xiao spoke of your force and foresight—that is why this commandery was set in your hands.」

sentences.zh: 榮祖善彈，彈鳥毛盡而鳥不死。

translations.literal: Rongzu was skilled with the sling; he could strike a bird so that every feather fell yet the bird did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu was master of the sling; he could strike a bird until every feather fell and still leave it alive.

sentences.zh: 海鵠羣翔，榮祖登城西樓彈之，無不折翅而下。

translations.literal: When flocks of sea geese wheeled in flight, Rongzu mounted the west gate tower and shot at them; none failed to break wing and fall.
translations.idiomatic: When sea geese flocked overhead he climbed the west gate tower and slung at them—not one failed to break wing and drop from the sky.

sentences.zh: 除晉熙王征虜、安成王車騎中兵，左軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was made a soldier of the expeditionary force under the Prince of Jinxi and the chariot force under the Prince of Ancheng, and left-army general.
translations.idiomatic: He was named soldier of the expeditionary staff under the Prince of Jinxi and of the chariot force under the Prince of Ancheng, and made left-army general.

sentences.zh: 元徽末，太祖欲渡廣陵，榮祖諫曰：「領府去臺百步，公走，人豈不知。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhui the Grand Ancestor wished to cross to Guangling; Rongzu remonstrated: 「The chief's residence is a hundred paces from the capital platform; if my lord flees, will men not know?
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yuanhui the Grand Ancestor meant to flee across to Guangling; Rongzu warned him: 「Your headquarters stand a hundred paces from the throne hall—if you run, who will not know?

sentences.zh: 若單行輕騎，廣陵人一旦閉門不相受，公欲何之？

translations.literal: If you travel alone with light cavalry, the men of Guangling may one day shut their gates and refuse you—where would my lord go?
translations.idiomatic: Ride out alone with a light escort, and Guangling may shut its gates on you—where then can you go?

sentences.zh: 公今動足下牀，便恐卽有扣臺門者，公事去矣。

translations.literal: If my lord now steps off the couch, I fear men will at once knock at the capital gate—my lord's business is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Set foot off your couch now, and I fear someone will be beating on the palace gate—your cause is finished.

sentences.zh: 」及蒼梧廢，除寧朔將軍、淮南太守，進輔國將軍，除游擊將軍、太祖驃騎諮議，輔國將軍、西中郎司馬、汝陰太守，除冠軍將軍，給事中，驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: 」When Cangwu was deposed, he was made General Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Huainan, promoted to General Who Assists the State; made General Who Raids in Pincer Formation and counselor on the Grand Ancestor's Rapid Cavalry staff; General Who Assists the State, Western Army Major, and Administrator of Ruyin; made General Who Champions the State, attendant within the Yellow Gates, and General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: 」After Cangwu was removed, he became general who pacifies the north and administrator of Huainan, then general who assists the state; he took the post of raiding general and counselor on the Grand Ancestor's rapid-cavalry staff, kept as assisting general, western army major, and administrator of Ruyin; then champion general, attendant within the yellow gates, and valiant-cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 預佐命勳，封將樂縣子，三百戶，以其祖舊封封之。

translations.literal: For merit in aiding the founding mandate he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jiangle with three hundred households, the old fief of his grandfather being conferred again.
translations.idiomatic: Credited in the founding merit rolls, he was enfeoffed as viscount of Jiangle, three hundred households, with his grandfather's former fief restored to the line.

sentences.zh: 出爲持節、督青冀二州刺史，冠軍如故。

translations.literal: Sent out as holder of the staff of authority and supervisor of the two provinces Qing and Ji, his rank as champion general unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He went out bearing the staff of authority as supervisor of Qing and Ji, still champion general.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門郎。

translations.literal: He was moved to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to gentleman at the yellow gates.

sentences.zh: ，爲冠軍將軍、尋陽相、南新蔡太守。

translations.literal: , made General Who Champions the State, Chancellor of Xunyang, and Administrator of Southern Xin'ai.
translations.idiomatic: , named champion general, chancellor of Xunyang, and administrator of southern Xin'ai.

sentences.zh: 作大形棺材盛仗，使郷人田天生、王道期載渡江北。

translations.literal: He had a large coffin-shaped chest made to hold weapons and had fellow townsmen Tian Tiansheng and Wang Daoqi carry it across the Yangtze to the north.
translations.idiomatic: He had a great coffin-shaped chest built for arms and set fellow townsmen Tian Tiansheng and Wang Daoqi to ferry it north of the river.

sentences.zh: 監奴有罪，告之，有司奏免官削爵付東冶，案驗無實見原。

translations.literal: A supervised slave committed an offense and informed on him; the authorities memorialized to strip his office and title and send him to the Eastern Works; investigation found no substance and he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: A household slave under supervision offended and denounced him; the court moved to dismiss him, strip his rank, and hand him to the eastern workshops—but inquiry found nothing and he was restored.

sentences.zh: 爲安陸王平西諮議，帶江陵令，仍遷司馬、河東內史。

translations.literal: Made counselor on the Prince of Pingxi's western staff, concurrently Magistrate of Jiangling; then moved to Major and Interior Minister of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He became counselor on the Prince of Pingxi's western staff with concurrent magistracy of Jiangling, then major and interior minister of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 遷持節、督緣淮諸軍事、冠軍將軍、兖州刺史，領東平太守、兖州大中正。

translations.literal: Moved to holder of the staff of authority, supervisor of armies along the Huai borderlands, General Who Champions the State, Inspector of Yan Province, concurrently Administrator of Dongping and chief rectifier of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to bearer of the staff, supervisor of armies along the Huai frontier, champion general and inspector of Yan, with concurrent administration of Dongping and chief rectifier of Yan.

sentences.zh: 巴東王子響事，方鎮皆啓稱子響爲逆，榮祖曰：「此非所宜言。

translations.literal: In the affair of the Prince of Badong Zi Xiang, every regional commander memorialized calling Zi Xiang a rebel; Rongzu said: 「This is not what ought to be said.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Badong, Zi Xiang, was implicated, every frontier commander wrote in calling him a rebel; Rongzu said, 「That is not how this should be put.

sentences.zh: 政應云劉寅等孤負恩獎，逼迫巴東，使至於此。

translations.literal: One should only say that Liu Yin and others betrayed imperial grace and favor, pressed hard upon the Prince of Badong, and drove matters to this pass.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial should say only that Liu Yin and his fellows betrayed the court's grace, harried the prince of Badong, and forced events to this point.

sentences.zh: 」時諸啓皆不得通，事平後，上乃省視，以榮祖爲知言。

translations.literal: 」At the time none of the memorials could get through; after the affair was settled, the emperor then reviewed them and judged Rongzu to speak with insight.
translations.idiomatic: 」None of those submissions reached him at the time; when the crisis ended the emperor read them through and called Rongzu's wording wise.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he died, aged fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 從父閎，宋孝建初，爲威遠將軍、汝南新蔡太守，據梁山拒丞相義宣賊，以功封西都縣子。

translations.literal: His father's younger brother Hong—in the beginning of Xiaojian in Song was General Who Overawes the Distant and Administrator of Runan and Xin'ai, held Liang Mountain against the rebel minister of works Yixuan, and for merit was enfeoffed as Viscount of Xidu.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Hong, at the opening of Song's Xiaojian reign, was general who overawes the distant and administrator of Runan and Xin'ai; he held Liang Mountain against the rebel minister of works Yixuan and was enfeoffed viscount of Xidu for the service.

sentences.zh: 累遷龍驤將軍、司州刺史。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to General Who Soars as Dragon and Inspector of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to dragon-soaring general and inspector of Si.

sentences.zh: 義嘉事起，明帝使閎出守盱眙，領兵北討薛道標，破之。

translations.literal: When the Yijia affair arose, Emperor Ming sent Hong out to guard Xuyi and lead troops north to attack Xue Daobiao, defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yijia crisis broke out, Emperor Ming posted Hong to guard Xuyi and march north against Xue Daobiao, whom he defeated.

sentences.zh: 封樂郷縣男，三百戶。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Yuexiang with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed baron of Yuexiang, three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 昇明初，爲散騎常侍，領長水校尉，與豫章王對直殿省，遷右衞將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengming he was made Cavalier Attendant-at-Large, concurrently Commandant of the Ever-Flowing Waters, paired with the Prince of Yuzhang in attending the palace halls, and moved to General of the Right Guards.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shengming he became cavalier attendant-at-large with concurrent command of the ever-flowing waters, shared palace duty with the Prince of Yuzhang, and was shifted to general of the right guards.

sentences.zh: 太祖卽位，以心誠封爵如舊，加給事中，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor took the throne, in recognition of sincere loyalty his rank and fief were kept as before; he was added Attendant Within the Yellow Gates and concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At the Grand Ancestor's accession his rank and fief stood unchanged for proved loyalty; he was given attendant within the yellow gates and concurrent valiant-cavalry command.

sentences.zh: 累遷金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Grand Master with Golden Bell and Purple Canopy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to grand master with golden bell and purple canopy.

sentences.zh: 年七十六，，卒，諡定。

translations.literal: Aged seventy-six, , he died; posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy-six he died; posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 榮祖從弟歷生，亦爲驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Rongzu's younger male cousin Lisheng also served as General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu's cousin Lisheng likewise held command as valiant-cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始初，薛安都反，以女婿裴祖隆爲下邳太守，歷生時請假還北，謀殺祖隆，舉城應朝廷，事發奔走。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi in Song, Xue Andu rebelled and made his son-in-law Pei Zulong Administrator of Xiapi; Lisheng was then on leave returning north and plotted to kill Zulong and raise the city in response to the court; the plot broke and he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Song's Taishi reign Xue Andu rebelled and installed his son-in-law Pei Zulong as administrator of Xiapi; Lisheng was home on leave in the north, plotted to kill Zulong and hand the city to the throne, but the scheme leaked and he ran.

sentences.zh: 歷官太子右率。

translations.literal: His offices included Right Leader of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Among his posts was right leader of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 性苛暴，好行鞭捶。

translations.literal: By nature he was harsh and violent, fond of applying the whip.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh and violent by nature, he loved the lash.

sentences.zh: 與始安王遙光同反，伏誅。

translations.literal: He joined the Prince of Shi'an Yao Guang in rebellion and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Shi'an, Yao Guang, in revolt and was put to death.

translations.literal: Appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：太祖作牧淮、兖，始基霸業，恩威北被，感動三齊。

translations.literal: The historian writes: When the Grand Ancestor governed Huai and Yan, he first laid the foundation of the hegemonic enterprise; grace and awe reached northward and moved the Three Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: As the Grand Ancestor held Huai and Yan he first set the base of empire; favor and dread spread north and stirred the Three Qi.

sentences.zh: 青、冀豪右，崔、劉望族，先睹人雄，希風結義。

translations.literal: The great houses of Qing and Ji, the Cui and Liu clans of eminent lineage, saw the hero first and yearned for his wind to bind themselves in righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and Ji's great families, the Cui and Liu lines of standing, saw the rising man early and, drawn by his manner, pledged themselves in faith.

sentences.zh: 夫諫江都之略，似任光之言，雖議不獨興，理成合契，蓋帷幙之臣也。

translations.literal: His remonstrance against the Guangling plan resembles Ren Guang's words; though the counsel did not arise alone, reason and fact fitted together—he was a man of the curtain camp.
translations.idiomatic: Counsel against the Guangling move recalls Ren Guang; though the advice was not his alone, the logic matched events—he was a counselor of the camp curtain.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：淮鎮北州，獲在崔、劉。

translations.literal: In praise: The Huai garrison, the northern province—success lay in Cui and Liu.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Huai's garrison, the northern command—the prize was Cui and Liu.

sentences.zh: 獻書上議，帝念忠謀。

translations.literal: Submitting memorials with policies above—the emperor kept their loyal stratagems in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials and counsel sent up—the throne remembered their loyal designs.

sentences.zh: 侃奉潛躍，皇瑞是鳩。

translations.literal: Kan upheld the hidden rise—the imperial auspice was gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Kan served the hidden ascent—the royal omen was gathered in.

sentences.zh: 垣方帶礪，削免虛尤。

translations.literal: Yuan's fief bears stone and whetstone; stripping and pardon voided empty blame.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's investiture bore stone and whetstone; dismissal and remission cleared false charges.
